records.name: 1 good thing
records.description:
Some days feel too small to remember. 1 good thing is where you keep them anyway.

Draw one good thing, in seconds. Drop it in the jar.

records.name: ArtMyVibe
records.description: Most galleries sort by artist, date and school. This one sorts by feeling — describe a mood, or just type what’s on your mind, and it finds the paintings that fit. Over 10,000 public-domain paintings.

records.name: Been there
records.description: A collection of places you’ve been to or called home, told through embroidered patches.

records.name: Chute
records.description: Turn your Mac's notch into a super fast Airdrop portal to your iPhone.

records.name: Huddlekit
records.description: Website feedback tool

records.name: Iris
records.description: A tool for extracting colours from an image.

records.name: Lunagraph
records.description: Full-featured design canvas that runs on code. Design, explore, refine by hand, then hand off the whole experience. States, interactions, and flows, all as React code.

records.name: Porcelain tic-tac-toe
records.description: A browser-based porcelain atelier where you paint one quarter of a tic-tac-toe board, let symmetry complete it, then turn the digital design into a handmade ceramic piece.

records.name: Resurf
records.description: One place for your ideas, references, and inspiration.

records.name: Rows
records.description: its not mine (i didnt build it) im just a big fan. yall should also check out respiro by @sgnoogle (such GREAT design OMFG)

records.name: Type Foundry Directory
records.description: An index of type foundries organized to help demystify font licensing and make searching for type easier.

records.name: TypeStax
records.description: TypeStax is a type scale builder for designers working on design systems, that feels like vintage audio hardware.

records.name: Bekadoo
records.description: A Pomodoro timer with ambient scenes and white noise. Choose a city and setting, set a focus session from 5 to 60 minutes, and add music from YouTube or Spotify.

records.name: Colors & Fonts
records.description: Build color palettes, test contrast, pair fonts, and create mesh gradients and shaders. Export the results for use in your designs.

records.name: doppio
records.description: Create motion pieces from templates in a dedicated editor. Add your designs and adjust the template controls to make animated presentations of your work.

records.name: FlingWords
records.description: Type words and fling them around the screen. This iPhone toy uses physics to make letters bounce and collide.

records.name: FlipNote
records.description: Send messages from your phone to a shared split-flap display on a TV, tablet, or browser. Create a board for notes and reminders at home, at work, or at an event.

records.name: Frownie
records.description: A Mac menu bar app that detects when you frown and reminds you to relax your forehead.

records.name: Hands Time
records.description: Clock widgets for iPhone with a choice of themes and visual styles.

records.name: Mac Harmonium
records.description: Play harmonium notes in your browser with the A through J keys. Drag the bellows with your mouse, or use the lid sensor on a compatible MacBook to pump air.

records.name: Make Your Own Breakfast
records.description: Browse breakfast recipes shared by the community. The iOS app suggests meals using the ingredients you have.

records.name: Mat
records.description: Arrange photo cutouts and stickers on a digital cutting mat, then display your collage as a Home Screen widget.

records.name: Momotaro: App Blocker
records.description: Set a focus timer that blocks distracting apps during a session. Complete sessions to unlock additional color themes.

records.name: Oddflick
records.description: Discover classic films through short clips, then tap to watch the full movie. Browse by genre or decade, save a watchlist, and resume where you left off. Available for iPhone.

records.name: Odorne
records.description: Browse homes from around the world and find the furniture, lighting, and other products featured in each room.

records.name: Pixelmon
records.description: A browser game with Game Boy-style graphics where you play as a designer, product manager, or engineer and battle for buy-in.

records.name: Powst
records.description: Find UK businesses by type and location, design a postcard, and send it by post. Preview the design and price before checkout.

records.name: rotation
records.description: Explore music charts on an interactive globe. Select a country or city to hear what is playing there, or follow curated routes across regions.

records.name: Toolcraft
records.description: An open-source starter kit and UI library for building design apps with AI. Use its components to create creative tools, internal utilities, and interactive experiments.

records.name: Uni
records.description: A desktop assistant for macOS and Windows that answers questions, transcribes speech, and provides quick actions from a panel near your cursor.

records.name: Jelly Dice
records.description: Roll one to five squishy 3D dice in your browser. Choose from six jelly styles, tap a die to poke it, or drag to stretch it before rolling.

records.name: Archiv
records.description: A collection app for identifying and organizing objects from the world around you. Turn photos of everyday finds into a visual archive, browse by category, and adjust the collection grid to suit your view.

records.name: DialKit
records.description: Add a control panel to your React project and adjust motion, layout, colors, and other values in real time. Use sliders, toggles, and presets to explore variations while seeing the result directly in your interface.

records.name: Loot
records.description: Photograph something you love and Loot identifies it, removes the background, and adds it to a collection. Organize everyday finds, collect with friends, and share collections or export them as posters from your iPhone.

records.name: Murmur
records.description: An open-source collection of animated glass orbs for AI interfaces, with web and SwiftUI versions. Explore visual styles, tune their appearance, and switch between states such as listening, thinking, and responding.

records.name: Pica
records.description: A free, native macOS font manager with custom collections, logo and color previews, and one-click font activation. Explore OpenType features, watch folders for new fonts, and work with Chinese, Japanese, and Korean type.

records.name: Weather OS
records.description: An interactive weather simulator for shaping clouds, storms, fog and snow with tactile controls, turning a full-screen sky into a playful study of atmospheric motion.

records.name: Letters of Love
records.description: A weekend project reviving the art of the love letter: a small, beautifully typeset collection of notes across time, made to inspire writing to your beloved.

records.name: Use Shelf
records.description: A browser extension that sends links and selected text from Chrome or Safari to a private Telegram bot chat in one click, keeping saved references where you already collect them.

records.name: The Good Invoice
records.description: A live invoice builder for freelancers and small studios, with editable client details, line items, taxes, notes, display options, logo upload and polished PDF export.

records.name: Annual Report Archive
records.description: An archive of 3,000+ annual reports from 1945–1991, revealing how companies once brought serious design, illustration, and artistry to their most ordinary publication.

records.name: Clocks
records.description: A customizable time and weather display for iPhone and iPad, pairing 13 clock styles with 28+ animated backgrounds as a daytime alternative to Apple’s StandBy mode.

records.name: Visitors
records.description: A revenue-first analytics service combining realtime traffic, visitor journeys, performance insights and funnels with privacy-friendly tracking and integrated payment attribution.

records.name: ASCIInator
records.description: A browser-based ASCII art generator that turns uploaded images into adjustable text compositions, with custom character ramps, sampling and tone controls, plus PNG, SVG and TXT export.

records.name: Whenever Works
records.description: A lightweight group-scheduling tool for creating date and time polls, sharing one link, collecting availability without accounts, and seeing which option works for the most people.

records.name: Slowday
records.description: A social city-discovery app that turns Instagram, TikTok and Google Maps links into saved places, building a personal map shaped by curators whose taste you trust.

records.name: Shake it to Shape it
records.description: A playful browser tool for generating geometric SVGs from randomized shapes, colors and styles, then copying or downloading the result for interfaces, identities and visual work.

records.name: Snackgood
records.description: A playful community snack guide where friends share fun, healthier finds with photos, stores and personal notes, turning everyday recommendations into a browsable visual collection.

records.name: DJR Glyphs
records.description: An interactive navigator through David Jonathan Ross’s type library for browsing individual glyphs across families, characters and variable-font instances, with links to each typeface.

records.name: Humanoid Index
records.description: A research index for browsing and comparing humanoid robots by company, country, dimensions, mobility, capabilities, price and production status, with detailed machine profiles.

records.name: Build Your Own Singaporean
records.description: A modular builder with local hairstyles, clothing, objects, skin tones and brand colours, helping anyone create distinctly Singaporean characters and scenes without design software.

records.name: Tracing Paper
records.description: A browser-based tracing workspace for layering reference images beneath translucent sheets, with grids, reveal regions and opacity controls for drawing studies and warmups.

records.name: BuilderTools
records.description: A curated showcase of experimental tools for designers and developers, documenting what each tool makes, the controls it offers and the independent builder behind it.

records.name: Silt
records.description: silt is the blackboard for designers who design in code: the real component, running and clickable, with every version and the session that made it kept together. a place, not a link.

records.name: Katalog
records.description: A social journal for logging, rating and discussing films, TV, books, albums and games in one place, with cross-format search, lists and Letterboxd or StoryGraph imports.

records.name: Curated Supply
records.description: A design-led directory of more than 1,000 useful, well-made objects across workspace, carry, coffee, audio and home, selected for material quality, utility and lasting design.

records.name: Warpbnb
records.description: A playful time-travel marketplace for browsing vacation rentals from ancient Egypt to a future Mars colony, with stays organized by theme, era and guest count.

records.name: Asterism
records.description: A Figma plugin for browsing Are.na without leaving the design canvas, bringing channels and visual references into the place where designers are already working.

records.name: Lyba
records.description: A review layer for Framer sites that lets clients pin comments directly to the live page, keeps feedback tied to exact screen sizes and records final approval.

records.name: Akuko Labs
records.description: An independent keyboard studio developing complete mechanical keyboards and keycap sets shaped by Bauhaus, photography and playful color, with projects ranging from Gestalt to Motif65.

records.name: Tracky
records.description: A playful project-management workspace for freelancers, combining project tracking with a notebook-style interface and a roadmap for tasks, to-dos, custom tables, reports and invoicing.

records.name: DeskSlope
records.description: A webcam-controlled 3D snowboarding game with a global leaderboard: lean to steer, crouch to brake, or play with arrow keys.

records.name: Ziney
records.description: Pick your paper and make a zine: an artsy browser zine editor with a public library of finished issues.

records.name: World Time Bestie
records.description: Plan across timezones by dragging city rows against a shared timeline, with date ranges and quick adds for every city you work with.

records.name: Cafe Pomodoro
records.description: Order a drink, settle in, and focus: a pomodoro timer dressed up as a cozy café, complete with ambient sound.

records.name: Ciggie Index
records.description: Enter a city and hours spent outside to see your local air quality translated into cigarettes smoked.

records.name: Shrump
records.description: A webcam-powered posture nagger that catches you mid-slouch.

records.name: Weatherbunny
records.description: An outfit helper that tells you what to wear for today's weather, so you never over- or under-dress again.

records.name: Design Your Sunset
records.description: A sunset-gradient generator for designers: tune warmth, glow and haze with live presets, then copy the CSS or download your wallpaper at desktop, tablet, or phone sizes.

records.name: Nostalgic Snacks
records.description: A draggable, explorable museum of Malaysia's most nostalgic snacks, from White Rabbit Candy to Haw Flakes, with photos, details, and a "where's mine?" submission flow.

records.name: ShaderGradient
records.description: Create living, animated gradients and drop them straight into Figma, Framer, or your React app. Tune shape, colors and motion on the web, then ship them anywhere.

records.name: Textures
records.description: Drop in any image and run it through 25 tactile filters, from Risograph to Cyanotype, then download the result at full resolution. Free, instant, no signup.

records.name: Color Shift
records.description: Pull color inspiration from randomly loaded Unsplash photos and check every background and foreground pairing live against WCAG and APCA contrast standards. A free iOS companion from Shift Nudge, the interface design training by Matt D. Smith.

records.name: Zoah
records.description: A collaborative platform for designing, versioning, and publishing code components from a visual canvas, with branching, diffs, merging, and AI. Formerly Opacity. Currently accepting waitlist signups.

records.name: Orbkit
records.description: A React library of WebGL shader orbs for AI and voice interfaces. Preview idle, thinking, and speaking states, tune each orb in the playground, and install components through the shadcn registry to customize them in your own project.

records.name: Holo Sticker
records.description: A Figma plugin that turns selected layers into holographic stickers. Choose tinted, rainbow, glitter, or foil finishes, adjust the shimmer and die-cut edges, and add the result back to your file as an image. Supports multiple layers at once.

records.name: Drawably
records.description: A lightweight library of hand-drawn UI controls for React and plain JavaScript. Buttons, inputs, cards, and text decorations generate fresh pen sketches, with subtle CSS animation and real form controls underneath.

records.name: Centered rounded CTA panel by AdScope
records.description: A quiet, high-contrast call-to-action section that uses generous whitespace, centered alignment, and a single dark pill button to create a clear next step without visual competition.

records.name: FAQ-to-CTA transition by AdScope
records.description: This section pairs a quiet, bordered FAQ row with a high-contrast CTA reveal, creating a clear transition from resolving hesitation to taking action. The only element is a single centred lockup on both axes — a multicolour segmented ring with a white inner disc holding a black ECG-pulse glyph, paired with a lowercase near-black geometric-sans wordmark that carries a faint warm fade toward its lower right. No headline, tagline or URL competes for attention; roughly 40% of the canvas stays empty, and the dark-on-pastel contrast keeps the card legible at the small sizes chat apps render shared links.

records.name: AirPods 5 product landing page by AirPods 5
records.description: A full-length Apple product page that alternates between immersive full-bleed gradient "scenes" (orange/blue ANC, magenta audio, teal/green charging) and clean white editorial sections. The rhythm works by shifting colour temperature every act: a cinematic hero, a tight highlight card carousel, a product close-up strip, then colour-blocked feature acts with centred eyebrow-label headlines, followed by horizontal card carousels, a stats trio, a services band, and a two-column comparison finish. Type is strictly two-tier (huge semibold display + small supporting copy), with horizontal carousels and eyebrow labels doing the navigational work.

records.name: AirPods 5 social card by AirPods 5
records.description: A 1200×630 Open Graph card built on a single floating studio photograph: two white earbuds rendered large in the centre with soft diffuse shadows, against a flat near-white (#f5f5f7) field. There is no text baked into the image — hierarchy is created entirely by the oversized centred product at roughly 55% of canvas height, letting the link preview supply the headline. The treatment relies on luminous whites, subtle grey gradients on the product, and tiny dark accents (the black mesh grilles and "R" marking) providing contrast; the mood is clinical, calm and premium through pure whitespace.

records.name: Anthropic landing page by anthropic.com
records.description: An editorial, typographically driven landing page built on a warm parchment background with stark black full-bleed sections as rhythm breaks. The hero pairs a bold underlined grotesk headline with a right-aligned serif paragraph, an asymmetric two-column split. Down the page, density increases: a sparse dark product announcement, three beige release cards with tabular date/category metadata, a two-column statement-plus-index list with hairline dividers, and a massive multi-column dark footer. Serif display type against sans body text, generous whitespace, and minimal ornamentation carry the identity.

records.name: Anthropic minimal wordmark social card by anthropic.com
records.description: A radically restrained 1200×630 social card: a warm paper off-white field carries nothing but the brand wordmark, set in bold letter-spaced uppercase and centered as a single focal point. The only gesture is the wordmark's own backslash detail, which doubles as visual interest; all hierarchy comes from scale and negative space. Colour is reduced to one near-black on one warm ivory, making the card read instantly at thumbnail size in a feed.

records.name: Arc browser landing page by arc.net
records.description: The page alternates saturated colour bands — a textured cobalt for nav, press quote and closing CTA, warm peach-to-pink gradients for the hero, and cream panels for the press ticker and community quotes — all joined by signature zigzag edges. Feature sections on white follow one strict rhythm: a short cobalt rounded-sans heading with a grey subline, then a single oversized rounded product screenshot instead of feature grids. Social proof is split into a scrolling cream marquee of press quotes and a four-column wall of bold blue user quotes with handle pills, before the cobalt CTA and footer close the page on the same zigzag motif.

records.name: Arc OG social card — sticker logo on salmon grain by arc.net
records.description: This 1200×630 OG card is a single-object composition: the interlocking-loop 'A' mark sits dead centre, rendered as a die-cut sticker with a thick white border and soft shadow, floating on a flat salmon-pink field (~#F29EA4) with a fine grain overlay. There is no headline, wordmark or URL — the mark alone carries the brand, and gradient strokes (light-to-deep blue, coral-to-rose) give it dimension against the flat background. The ~65% negative space and radial symmetry make it instantly legible even at tiny link-preview thumbnail sizes.

records.name: Astro content-driven web framework landing page by astro.build
records.description: A dark, full-width developer-tools landing page uses a near-black navy canvas with large blue-purple gradients concentrated behind the hero and CTA panels. The page moves from a centered, high-contrast hero and dense customer logo wall into spacious explanatory sections, then increases information density through a performance comparison, framework selector, code/product preview, and a large asymmetric feature-card grid. Lower sections shift toward ecosystem proof—theme thumbnails, partner cards, sponsor tiles—and finish with a compact newsletter/footer grid, maintaining thin borders, restrained radii, and small magenta section labels throughout.

records.name: Astro OG social card by astro.build
records.description: A 1200×630 dark card split roughly 55/45: the left column carries the identity and message (small wordmark with logo mark, a two-line headline that switches from regular to heavy italic mid-sentence, and a rounded mascot icon with a gradient border), while the right half is a purely atmospheric field of blurred, glowing pills in purple, blue, teal, yellow, pink, orange and white, stacked like abstract code lines and bleeding off the canvas edge. A faint square grid texture and a violet ambient glow anchored in the lower left keep the dark background from reading flat. The single type move — regular-to-italic-bold emphasis — gives the card its personality without needing any extra decoration.

records.name: Attio agentic revenue CRM landing page by attio.com
records.description: A long-form CRM landing page that starts with a bright, spacious hero and progressively moves through product proof, feature modules, and customer evidence before switching into a high-contrast black platform section. The page uses oversized but restrained sans-serif headlines, pale blue-gray product backdrops, hairline grid rules, and dense UI screenshots; the lower half changes rhythm through dark architectural panels, then returns to white for scale metrics, case studies, changelog cards, and a compact newsletter footer.

records.name: Attio monochrome OG social card by attio.com
records.description: A 1200×630 card built on tension between two anchors: a chained run of five outlined isometric hexagonal prisms with dashed fold lines sits top-right like a packaging dieline or blueprint drawing, while a three-line headline drops down the bottom-left, each line one step lighter in gray until it nearly dissolves into the off-white ground. The wordmark is the only black element bottom-right, anchoring the diagonal flow from headline to logo. Faint dashed grid hairlines at the top-left edge expose the layout grid, giving the whitespace a technical, engineered feel rather than emptiness.

records.name: Basedash AI analyst landing page by Basedash in Español Français & Português
records.description: A warm paper-toned landing page (#f5f1ea) where airy, centered editorial headlines alternate with dense, hairline-bordered product mockups — a live BI dashboard with a chat panel, prompt-built charts, an audit log, and a 750-icon integration grid. Hierarchy is carried by a monospace orange micro-label system (trust badges, panel headers) plus serif italic testimonial quotes, giving the page a 'printed analyst report' feel. Rhythm builds from proof (logos, quotes) through capability demos to a security/compliance block, an FAQ accordion, and a closing CTA over a retro neon CRT visual, ending in a black footer.

records.name: Basedash OG social card — dark headline + dashboard mockup by Basedash in Español Français & Português
records.description: A 1200×630 social card split asymmetrically: a huge three-line white headline with a full stop anchors the left half, while a floating revenue-dashboard mockup card carries the proof on the right. Hierarchy is driven almost entirely by type scale and weight on a near-black ground, with violet and blue reserved exclusively for the chart lines and delta chips. The mockup is the only dense element — rounded corners, hairline border, faint warm wash at the top and two glowing data series — so the card reads as a single statement-plus-artifact composition at thumbnail size.

records.name: beehiiv newsletter platform landing page by beehiiv.com
records.description: A near-black canvas where hierarchy is carried entirely by type and colour: staccato all-caps grotesque headlines punctuated with periods, an electric-indigo highlight word in the hero, and hot-pink eyebrows and stat numerals. The middle of the page is a 2×3 bento grid of deep-indigo cards, each embedding a cropped, floating product-UI screenshot so features are shown rather than told. Below, rhythm alternates deliberately — dense creator/stat mosaic, structured four-column pricing with a subscriber slider, one airy quote panel, a punchy pink numbers band, an icon-tile integrations strip, a split FAQ — before a dense utility footer closes the page.

records.name: Beehiiv social card by beehiiv.com
records.description: A 1200×630 social card uses a near-black indigo canvas with faint oversized geometric forms behind the content. A small centered white wordmark anchors the top, while a two-line, extremely bold uppercase headline dominates the middle with a cool lavender-to-pink gradient; a thin divider and tightly spaced uppercase feature list create a footer band.

records.name: Betterment wealth management homepage by betterment.com
records.description: A finance landing page that pairs oversized editorial serif headlines with a restrained sans-serif UI layer. The opening uses a vivid blue photographic hero, then shifts through saturated blue product navigation, pale beige editorial sections, image-led proof points, and a deep navy footer; cards, statistics, FAQs, and disclosures progressively increase information density below the hero.

records.name: Betterment OG social card — centered wordmark lockup on blue gradient by betterment.com
records.description: A single-purpose social card built around one centered lockup: a yellow arch mark with a notched base sits left of the white 'Betterment' wordmark, both sized to fill the middle band of a 1200×630 canvas. The full-bleed background is a vertical blue gradient that darkens toward the bottom, giving depth without adding elements, and all remaining space is deliberately empty so the brand reads instantly at thumbnail size. Hierarchy comes purely from scale and contrast — the mark matches the wordmark's cap height, and the warm yellow-to-white pairing pops against the cool ground.

records.name: Bilt — Rent rewards landing page by bilt.com
records.description: Bilt's landing page is a long, cinematic dark page in near-black navy with a faint map-grid texture behind the hero, where left-aligned white serif headline text sits beside floating glassmorphic notification chips ("Ride with Lyft", "Dine out at Tucci") scattered over an aerial city. Below, a full-width night photograph of an apartment building hosts pill tab tabs (Rent/Neighborhood/Rewards) and a dark rent-summary card overlay. The page then develops in alternating rhythms: a 3-card feature row with photography and glass UI overlays (credit-score gauge, Rent Day card), a "Neighborhood Benefits" section with scattered photo tiles, category filter pills, and full-bleed dining photography columns with caption overlays; then a redemption section pairing left-aligned headings with logo-card carousels (airlines, hotels, Amazon, Walmart, Airbnb) under small horizontal rules; press-quote cards; a centered final CTA; and a minimal footer. Type is a light, wide sans-serif with generous letter spacing on huge headings; small caps labels, thin dividers, and pale-blue pill buttons provide the only color accents against the monochrome dark palette. Density is low with lots of negative space; every section breathes and the accent color is used sparingly for CTAs only.

records.name: Bilt rewards map social card by bilt.com
records.description: A portrait-format social card on a near-black navy canvas overlaid with a dimmed city street grid, so the map reads as texture rather than content. Four floating pill cards act as map annotations: three dark glass toasts with gold reward lines, plus one inverted pale-blue card ('You pay rent +2500 pts') that breaks the pattern and carries the focal message, each anchored by a tiny white dot. A two-tone grotesque headline anchors the lower-left — the first sentence in white, the remainder receding to slate blue — so hierarchy flows from the bright card down to the quiet type.

records.name: Blinkist homepage by blinkist.com
records.description: A consumer learning-app landing page built on a white canvas with a strict repeating pattern: oversized centred navy display headings, a bright green pill CTA anchoring every section, and flat pastel-filled cards that carry the colour. The hero splits mixed-weight headline type against overlapping phone mockups in a soft-blue panel with doodle stars; the page then alternates proof moments — an illustrated feature trio with video, a stat row, a chip cloud of interest topics, a book carousel, a lavender/cream feature carousel, photo testimonials with yellow-highlighted quotes, 95/91/87% claims, a pale-blue logo strip, a use-case photo quartet, an accordion FAQ — before ending in a near-black navy footer packed with small-type link columns. One rounded sans family, italic emphasis words, and completely flat surfaces (no borders or shadows) keep the long page coherent.

records.name: bolt.new AI app-builder landing page by bolt.new
records.description: A dark landing page where the product itself — a chat prompt box — is the hero CTA, floating on a large electric-blue glow orb with output-type tiles and start-from pills beneath it. The page then alternates quiet full-bleed statement sections with dense card clusters: greyed logo strip, a stat pair (98% less errors / 1000x), a deliberate mid-page colour shift into pink-purple for the design-system feature, a bento grid of 3D-rendered cloud-feature cards, and a persona grid using real product-UI screenshots. Type is a single grotesque sans at a wide scale range, with hierarchy built almost entirely from size, glow gradients and card depth on near-black surfaces; the closing CTA reuses the exact hero prompt module, then the footer dissolves into a giant striped wordmark.

records.name: bolt.new Open Graph social card by bolt.new
records.description: A 1200×630 dark social card split into a quiet left half and a product-teaser right half. The bolt.new wordmark sits large, bold and italicised on the left with a two-line gray tagline beneath, while the right half shows three stacked chat panels receding toward the top-right, cropped off the canvas edge to imply a bigger app. Depth is carried by a soft blue radial glow in the top-right corner and a sharp white light streak grazing the top edge of the rearmost panel; the frontmost panel reads as a prompt input with placeholder text and paperclip/sparkle icons. Type is a single sans family scaled in three steps — wordmark, tagline, UI text — with muted blue-gray on near-black doing all the contrast work.

records.name: Bun JavaScript runtime homepage by bun.sh
records.description: A long-form developer-tools landing page uses a mostly white canvas, hairline gray rules, oversized condensed black headlines, and hot pink accents to create a technical editorial feel. The hero establishes the product with a split text/benchmark layout, then the page alternates between compact card grids, large editorial feature bands, benchmark data, API/code demonstrations, a compatibility table, and a high-contrast black CTA footer; the rhythm shifts from dense evidence and comparison modules to spacious narrative sections.

records.name: Bun social card by bun.sh
records.description: A 1200×630 social card uses a white canvas with a compact top identity row: a cute rounded mascot at left and a large black wordmark beside it. The lower half is dominated by an oversized, tightly set sans-serif headline, with a single vivid pink phrase creating the focal accent; a small uppercase monospace capability line anchors the bottom edge.

records.name: bunq mobile banking landing page by bunq.com
records.description: A near-black, photography-led landing page where the rainbow brand gradient is deliberately confined to product imagery (phone screens, payment card) and soft ambient glows, so white type and spacing carry the structure. Rhythm alternates between left-aligned editorial blocks, centered section headers, full-bleed rounded photos, a hairline-divided feature accordion, and horizontally scrolling feature cards with a peeking next slide. Trust is stacked near the end: gradient stat banners in green, blue and orange, a monochrome press strip, starred review cards, and a Personal/Business segmented plan selector.

records.name: bunq 'Mobile banking made easy' social card by bunq.com
records.description: A 1200×630 share card built on an asymmetric split: the left ~55% is a quiet text zone over a deep navy vertical gradient, carrying a two-line headline in a heavy rounded geometric sans at roughly 96px, with a three-line trial-offer paragraph at about a third of that size directly beneath. The right side holds a photographic hand holding a slightly tilted phone that bleeds off the bottom-right corner; its screen of vertical rainbow stripes is the only saturated colour on the canvas, so the product becomes the focal point even though the type is far larger. Hierarchy comes purely from scale and contrast — no cards, borders, buttons or decorative elements, just generous padding and a soft shadow grounding the phone.

records.name: Cadenya agentic runtime landing page by Cadenya
records.description: The page runs a two-typeface system — a light uppercase display serif against small monospace labels — and threads a technical-drawing motif of 1px crop-mark corner brackets through every framed panel, diagram and photo. Rhythm comes from full-bleed background swaps down the page: off-white hero with a surreal floating bonsai island, a macro root photograph carrying two frosted-glass cards, deep forest-green panels with numbered node diagrams and an accordion/product-UI split, then a pale lime zone for FAQ before returning to white for the closing CTA and footer. The bonsai-on-island image recurs three times as a brand anchor, and a single lime accent (#D9E965-ish) marks focal diagram nodes, the highlighted phrase in the oversized statement, and interactive states.

records.name: Cal.com scheduling landing page by cal.com
records.description: A near-monochrome scheduling landing page built from white cards with hairline borders floating on an off-white canvas, where black is the only accent — reserved for CTAs, section badges and the selected calendar day. The hero pairs a three-line display headline and stacked auth buttons with a functional-looking booking widget (duration pills, timezone row, month grid), so the product demos itself above the fold. Below the hero the rhythm alternates between centred badge–headline–CTA sections and denser grids: three numbered step cards, a 2×2 bento of feature cards each embedding a real UI fragment (settings dropdowns, booking URL, mini week calendar, notification toast), an 8-tile icon grid, a masonry testimonial wall, an accordion FAQ and a final CTA with award laurels, closing on an unusually deep footer with platform download badges, compliance marks and multi-column links.

records.name: Cal.com social card — booking UI mockup by cal.com
records.description: A 1200×630 share card built as a cropped product shot: a light-grey canvas carries the wordmark alone in the top-right, while a large white rounded panel enters from the left and bleeds off the bottom edge. Inside the panel, a heavy two-line headline sits above a two-pane booking mockup — a lavender-to-deep-purple gradient banner with an avatar stack and event details on the left, a January calendar grid with rounded grey day chips on the right. The design works because the UI mockup does the storytelling: neutral grey framing, one saturated purple moment, and bold dark type at two sizes (wordmark and headline) with everything else small and quiet.

records.name: Cash App homepage hero by cash.app
records.description: The whole first viewport is a single flat field of vivid brand green — no gradient, texture or photography; colour alone carries the brand. The composition is a three-part split: an oversized two-line black grotesque headline left, a phone mockup of the live app centre-cropped by the hero's bottom edge, and a narrow ~30-character copy column with a white pill CTA right. Type does all the work (~88px headline against 14px body), buttons are all rounded pills in white or black, and the nav collapses to a squircle logo plus three controls. Below the hero the capture renders only white, so the page's visible design story ends at the fold — the hero is where the language lives.

records.name: Cash App OG social card by cash.app
records.description: A 1200×630 share card on a pure black field, deliberately left-weighted: the only element in the left half is a rounded-square app icon with a bold dollar glyph anchored bottom-left. The right two-thirds stacks two overlapping phone mockups — a white balance-list screen behind and a solid neon-green payment screen in front whose giant white '$20' numeral is the focal point — while a gold-flecked debit card bleeds off the bottom-right corner for texture. Hierarchy comes almost entirely from extreme scale contrast (the hero numeral is roughly eight times the UI label size), a single saturated accent carrying all brand colour, and edge-cropped props that imply a larger product beyond the frame.

records.name: ChatHop OG card — mascot surfing an arrow on black by ChatHop
records.description: A text-free social card where a pure black canvas lets one saturated chartreuse accent carry the entire composition. The focal point is a plump 3D blob mascot — oversized two-tone eyes, buck-tooth grin, black tube arms with white cartoon gloves — surfing a thick tapering lime arrow that sweeps diagonally from lower-left to upper-right, while two small speech-bubble puffs with typing dots anchor the upper corners. Hierarchy is built purely through scale and saturation rather than type, and the generous black negative space keeps the scene legible even at thumbnail size.

records.name: Chime fintech banking landing page by chime.com
records.description: A fintech landing page where a single deep forest-green surface carries almost the whole narrative: hero, feature explorer, bento pair, download panel and mission band are all variations of the same green, punctuated only by a black press marquee and one off-white interlude around the investing section. Hierarchy comes from extreme type scale (90px+ display headlines against 11px legal fine print) and a repeated green-check benefit list, while device mockups with live app UI and floating translucent info cards supply the proof. Below the hero the rhythm alternates full-bleed dark bands with white testimonial cards and a light editorial section, closing with an oversized mission statement behind a giant translucent wordmark and a five-column footer sunk in dense regulatory fine print.

records.name: Clay social card by clay.com
records.description: A 1200×630 social card uses a bright cyan sky and softly textured green landscape as a full-bleed illustrated backdrop. A dense arrangement of whimsical 3D objects creates the upper focal field, while the lower dark-green gradient clears visual space for a large centered white wordmark paired with a colorful arched icon.

records.name: Clerk authentication and user management landing page by clerk.com
records.description: A highly structured developer-facing landing page alternates bright white product sections with deep charcoal feature sections, using clipped angled transitions to make the long page feel segmented. Oversized black headlines, small purple or cyan eyebrow labels, restrained borders, soft shadows, and interface mockups establish hierarchy; the page moves from a sparse hero and logo strip into detailed component demonstrations, dense authentication and multi-tenancy feature grids, framework/integration panels, social proof, and a compact footer.

records.name: Clerk — Open Graph social card by clerk.com
records.description: A 1200×630 social card built on a near-black canvas with a radial blue glow rising from the right. Three layers carry the composition: a small white wordmark at top-left, a giant glossy 3D rendition of the C-shaped logo mark occupying the right half with a blue orb at its core, and a bold two-line headline anchored bottom-left where 'comprehensive' and 'Platform' shift to pale sky blue. Faint circuit-trace line art in the upper right adds texture without competing at thumbnail size. The diagonal reading path (wordmark → headline → artwork) and the stark scale contrast between the ~64px headline and the ~32px wordmark make it instantly legible in a 40px-tall link preview.

records.name: Cloudflare homepage — orange brand-block landing page by cloudflare.com
records.description: The page opens with a full-bleed, heavily rounded brand-orange hero panel — event pill, oversized two-line headline, one white pill CTA and a glowing horizon — then settles onto a white canvas where airy centred display statements alternate with dense proof modules: a halftone-dot globe card, a tabbed logo wall with testimonial, a bordered four-column pricing grid, and fake product-UI mockups (a deployment version table, an agent terminal). After the hero, orange is rationed to micro-accents — active tabs, "Deployed" badges, line icons — so the closing orange CTA band lands with the same visual weight as the opening. Thin 1px borders, flat shadows, a single geometric sans and a dense multi-column footer keep the enterprise scale readable.

records.name: Cloudflare "Start building" Open Graph card by cloudflare.com
records.description: A one-idea social card on a strict vertical axis: a small white cloud mark tops the frame, a fully rounded off-white capsule carries the two-word headline at dead centre, and a warm light glow rises from the bottom edge like a sunrise. The saturated orange field is enlivened by a faint repeating dot/glyph texture, so the background reads as designed rather than flat. All hierarchy comes from scale and value contrast — one bright capsule against one saturated field — with no supporting copy, URL or CTA to dilute the message.

records.name: Cognition SWE-2 research blog post by Cognition's SWE-2
records.description: A long-form research blog post rendered as a narrow single-column paper: small fixed left sidebar with sparse nav, a modest serif/mono-toned title block, then a dense flow of body text interleaved with custom data visualisations — Pareto-frontier line charts, grouped bar charts, a benchmark comparison table, and LaTeX-style math — each followed by small grey italic footnotes. The rhythm alternates text-paragraph blocks with wide, quietly coloured (blue/orange/green) figures; there are no cards, gradients or marketing sections, so authority comes from typographic restraint and figure quality. Sections are separated only by generous whitespace and heading size, and the page ends with numbered references and appendices like an academic preprint.

records.name: SWE-2 model announcement OG card by Cognition's SWE-2
records.description: A 1200×630 announcement card built almost entirely from one centered lockup on a near-black ground: a small kicker line sits above a huge tightly-tracked grotesque headline paired with a hexagonal logomark. Behind it, a faint white-on-black technical chart — ruler ticks, ruled horizontals and a fan of curves with tiny numerals and mirrored micro-labels — supplies depth without competing for attention. A subtle film-grain overlay and a strict black/white/gray palette make the giant type read as the only real subject.

records.name: Convex developer platform landing page by convex.dev
records.description: A full-width developer-platform landing page alternates a near-black hero and product sections with warm cream, olive, rust, and brown bands. The page starts with a compact split hero, oversized condensed headline, embedded command-style setup panel, and multicolour bent stripes; below it, proof becomes progressively denser through a trusted-by logo row, checklist and diagram, dark component cards, testimonials, founder credibility, enterprise strip, a grid-backed final CTA, and a multi-column footer.

records.name: Convex 'All Gas, No Breakages' OG social card by convex.dev
records.description: A 1200×630 social card that reads like a screen-printed poster: a warm cream field with a faint graph-paper grid, a two-line all-caps headline in a very heavy grotesque (~120px, line-height ≈0.95) pinned to the upper left, and a signature ribbon of flat stripes — amber, red-orange and purple nested inside a near-black L-shaped frame — running along the bottom before making one shared rounded 90° turn up the right edge. Focal order is headline → colour ribbon → cream-on-dark wordmark lockup in the bottom-left band. Everything is flat fill with no gradients, shadows or photography, so the black type and the three saturated stripe colours carry all the contrast.

records.name: Copilot Money landing page by copilot.money
records.description: A dark fintech landing page built on a near-black navy canvas with oversized pale-gray display type and a single vivid blue CTA colour. The hero's personality comes from tilted, emoji-stamped category pills floating around the headline, echoed again as a decorative strip above the footer. Mid-page, the design flips to a full-bleed light section for the wealth-tracking features, a hard rhythm break before returning to dark bento grids for pricing, a masonry wall of tweet-style testimonials, and a closing CTA with a device collage. Feature storytelling is done entirely through embedded UI mockups inside rounded cards — real charts, transaction lists and tickers rather than abstract illustrations.

records.name: Copilot Money OG social card by copilot.money
records.description: A 1200×630 social card built almost entirely on scale contrast: a three-line display headline in pale ice-blue dominates the left 55% of the canvas, set at roughly 120px with very tight leading, while a small logo lockup sits top-left and a one-line platform note anchors the bottom-left on the same margin. The right 45% is a diagonal cluster of iPhone, iPad and MacBook mockups, each rotated a few degrees and bleeding off the right and bottom edges, their dark-mode app screens (line charts, budget rings) providing the only saturated accents. Depth comes from a navy radial gradient plus soft shadows under the devices — no borders, cards or dividers anywhere.

records.name: Cortex API docs platform landing page by Cortex
records.description: A near-black developer-tool landing page that lets dense, dimmed product mockups carry the proof while typography stays minimal: a grotesque display headline with a deliberately dimmed second line, monospace uppercase eyebrows marked with dots and dashes, and hairline-bordered panels throughout. A single green accent is rationed to live dots, status chips, and checklist ticks, while HTTP method colors (green GET, blue POST, orange PUT, red DELETE) appear only inside the docs mockup. Rhythm alternates between centered hero-style sections and left-aligned feature blocks, compressed by full-width numbered table strips (spec surfaces, eleven languages) and a numbered bento grid of five proof cards.

records.name: Cron calendar landing page ("It's about time.") by cron.com
records.description: A near single-viewport dark landing page built around one massive white headline in a heavy grotesque, with a bright orange reserved for the logo, the sign-up pill and small UI accents in the product shots. The rhythm is announcement banner → oversized statement headline → one-line subcopy → a large composite desktop/mobile app screenshot. The product imagery does the persuading: a realistic dark calendar UI with a command palette open, warm orange event blocks, and an overlapping iPhone. The footer is a single quiet row of text links, keeping the page to one confident idea.

records.name: Cursor coding agent landing page by cursor.com
records.description: A restrained developer-tools landing page uses a wide, low-contrast header and a large open hero field to make the concise product statement carry the hierarchy. Black and soft gray pill buttons create clear action priority, while the oversized desktop-app screenshot introduces visual density and a warm photographic backdrop below the fold.

records.name: Cursor OG social card by cursor.com
records.description: A link-preview card reduced to its absolute minimum: a near-black canvas (roughly 1200×630) with a single white lockup dead-center, both horizontally and at optical vertical center. The mark is a hexagonal cube whose interior is cut away so a cursor arrow appears in negative space; the wordmark CURSOR sits to its right in an extended, all-caps geometric sans with wide tracking, sized so the letter height matches the mark. Focal hierarchy comes purely from scale and contrast — no tagline, URL, gradient, or decoration anywhere, which keeps it legible even when the card renders at thumbnail size. The vast empty field is the actual design decision: it makes the small white lockup feel deliberate and confident rather than sparse.

records.name: DataFast revenue analytics landing page by datafa.st
records.description: A long, conversion-focused analytics landing page uses a warm off-white canvas, near-black typography, and a restrained coral-orange accent for every primary action. The hero is sparse and centered, then the page becomes progressively denser through dashboard imagery, testimonial feeds, three-step cards, feature tiles, integrations, pricing, FAQ, and a final CTA/footer; repeated framed screenshots and soft shadows create continuity across the changing rhythms.

records.name: Datafast OG social card — headline + chart card by datafa.st
records.description: A 1200×630 social card built on a warm cream canvas with a single centred vertical stack: five golden stars, a one-line bold benefit headline, and a large white chart card that bleeds off the bottom edge. The chart does the branding work — organic, uneven coral bars with rounded tops sit under a wavy sky-blue area line, and a stat row ('5.4k visitors • $2,325 revenue') pairs bold dark numbers with gray labels. Hierarchy comes purely from scale and weight contrast on neutrals; three soft accents (coral, sky blue, gold) carry all the colour, and the off-white background makes the white card read as a floating product screenshot.

records.name: Deno runtime landing page by deno.com
records.description: A developer-focused landing page alternates a restrained white documentation-like canvas with deep charcoal feature bands, using bright mint green for badges, buttons, highlights, and active code states. The page starts with a compact announcement and navigation, then moves from a dark split hero into installation commands, code-led capability sections, security cards, benchmark grids, deployment integrations, social proof, and a final product CTA; the rhythm broadens from dense technical proof to spacious editorial blocks before resolving in a dark multi-column footer.

records.name: Deno OG social card — 'is your JavaScript runtime' by deno.com
records.description: A 1200×630 social card built as one continuous sentence: a bold lowercase wordmark plus 'is your' anchors the left column at vertical centre, while the right column stacks ten capability terms in heavy grotesque type. Selection is communicated purely through opacity — terms fade to near-white toward the top and bottom edges like a carousel frozen mid-scroll — and the chosen term 'JavaScript runtime' sits on a full-bleed mint-green highlight bar in near-black type, making it the single focal point. The background is a quiet white-to-pale-blue vertical gradient with no decoration, letting the typographic contrast and one saturated accent carry the whole message.

records.name: Descript AI video editor landing page by descript.com
records.description: Descript's homepage is a long editorial marketing page that alternates deep-maroon and near-black bands with cream trust bands. A floating white pill nav sits over a hero set in an oversized cream serif headline, with red letter-spaced eyebrow labels and a single red CTA; proof comes from large editor mockups including a floating AI-chat card. Down the page the rhythm shifts through a logo marquee, three dark testimonial cards, a tabbed numbered workflow slide (01 Record) with prev/next arrows, an AI-tools carousel, a 01–06 use-case switcher, then cream bands holding compliance badges, oversized stat numerals, lavender review cards, a split FAQ accordion, and a dense four-column footer with a secondary guides/tools panel. The high-contrast serif paired with a neutral grotesque and a strictly reserved red accent hold all thirteen sections together.

records.name: Descript OG social card by descript.com
records.description: A 1200×630 social card staged on a single deep-burgundy field with no gradient or texture. The top third holds a three-line, sentence-case serif headline in cream with tight leading and terminal periods; the centre is a white product screenshot flanked by video-still strips that bleed off both canvas edges like a timeline, one small circular avatar overlapping on the right. The rhythm runs quiet–busy–quiet, with colour rationed to the burgundy stage, cream type, and a single red accent reserved for the logo mark above the lowercase sans wordmark.

records.name: Desert Ant Labs — on-device AI model library landing page by Desert Ant Labs
records.description: A warm cream editorial landing page where an enormous tight grotesque headline (first line distressed with a spray-paint texture) sits over tiny monospace body copy — the size contrast is the whole hierarchy. Colour is withheld until a full-bleed carousel of slightly rotated, duotone-pastel model cards, after which the page settles into a dense three-column grid of flat beige model cards with mono uppercase tag pills, a punchy free-tier CTA with pill buttons, and a six-column mono-labelled footer. Rhythm alternates airy statements with dense card clusters down the page, and beta models are signalled by greyed-out text plus small Beta badges in both grid and footer.

records.name: Desert Ant Labs social card by Desert Ant Labs
records.description: A roughly 1200×630 off-white social card uses a sparse, left-anchored composition with generous negative space. A small black rounded-square mark sits in the upper-left, while the focal headline occupies the lower-left in two oversized lines: the first has a soft grainy texture and the second is crisp, heavy black type; a small monospaced URL provides a quiet footer detail.

records.name: DockFix 5.0 landing page by DockFix 5.0
records.description: The page opens on a full-bleed, desaturated moorland photograph with the product name set as an oversized black grotesque wordmark, then alternates cream editorial sections, black inverted bands and further photo bands as chapter breaks down the page. Hierarchy is built almost entirely from extreme type-scale jumps, huge whitespace tracts and 1px hairline rules — the feature list is a two-column label/description table with no cards — while a single coral-red accent is reserved for buttons, the price and one eyebrow label. A black four-column stats strip, a photo band carrying a three-line manifesto statement, and a giant low-contrast footer watermark give the page its rhythm; the long cream tracts are scroll-animation stages for product demos.

records.name: DockFix 5.0 Open Graph social card by DockFix 5.0
records.description: A 1200×630 social card built like an Apple keynote slide: a muted terracotta hillside under a pale blue sky, with a giant black wordmark layered so the horizon ridge slightly occludes its lower edge, giving flat type real depth. The product itself is rendered in place — a glassmorphic macOS-style dock with placeholder-sized icons and widgets sits on the bottom edge like a stage prop. Hierarchy is handled by extreme scale contrast (display wordmark vs. a tiny tracked-out red 'OUT NOW · €14.99' eyebrow) and by confining everything to three strict horizontal bands: metadata, headline, product.

records.name: Domestika creative courses homepage by domestika.org
records.description: A commerce-led education homepage combines a dark utility navigation with a vivid orange urgency banner and a blue promotional hero. Below the hero, the page becomes highly scannable: four-column course cards repeat a tight image, metadata, discount, and teal purchase-button pattern, then shift into teacher discovery, a sparse benefits grid, and a text-heavy SEO footer. Orange is reserved for promotion and primary calls to action, while teal handles repeated buying actions against a mostly white, lightly bordered canvas.

records.name: Domestika OG social card — white wordmark on flat red field by domestika.org
records.description: A single-element social card: a full-bleed flat red-orange field (~#F02A10) with nothing but the white DOMÉSTIKA wordmark, optically centred on the 1200×630 canvas. Roughly 85% of the surface is empty colour, so the heavy geometric sans wordmark — whose accented É is doubled by the brand's chevron glyph — carries all focal weight. The restraint works because contrast does everything: one saturated hue, one pure-white wordmark at ~55% of canvas width, no tagline, URL, imagery or second colour to dilute recognition in a small link preview.

records.name: Drizzle Team open-source org page by drizzle.team
records.description: A near-monochrome open-source org page where the data does the design work: eleven project cards each pair a star/fork count with a black sparkline charting traction over time. Structure is carried by tiny uppercase micro-labels and a two-line black/grey greeting, and the rhythm shifts down the page from a dense three-column card grid to a heavy light-grey sponsor panel and a sparse three-column footer. Colour is withheld almost entirely — white, greys, one dark button — leaving a single blue 'Become a sponsor' link as the only action accent.

records.name: Duolingo landing page by duolingo.com
records.description: A playful, illustration-driven landing page built almost entirely on white space and a single saturated green accent. The hero pairs a floating character cluster with a short headline and two stacked pill buttons; a scrolling strip of language/course chips acts as a divider. Below, four feature sections alternate text and illustration left/right in a strict rhythm — each has a bold lowercase green heading, one short grey paragraph, and a colourful cartoon. Rhythm shifts mid-page: a centred, confetti-like "learn anytime, anywhere" app section breaks the alternating pattern, then a full-bleed navy band for the premium tier provides the page's single dark contrast moment. It closes with an English Test feature, a centred CTA, a wavy green footer transition into a dense multi-column link footer. Hierarchy comes from scale and colour contrast (green headings vs grey body) rather than borders or shadows.

records.name: ElevenLabs AI audio platform landing page by elevenlabs.io
records.description: A long, highly structured AI platform homepage uses a near-white canvas, thin gray dividers, restrained black typography, and rounded product panels to keep a large amount of content calm and legible. The hero moves quickly from a compact navigation and two-column headline into a tactile audio-product carousel, then the rhythm alternates between logo proof, platform overviews, dense bento feature grids, API/code panels, media cards, research storytelling, safety principles, updates, and a large multi-column footer. Colour is mostly monochrome UI chrome, with soft blurred orange, blue, green, purple, and red gradients reserved for audio imagery, editorial cards, and feature emphasis.

records.name: ElevenLabs wordmark-over-warped-grid OG card by elevenlabs.io
records.description: A 1200×630 social card built around a single focal element: the "ElevenLabs" wordmark with its "II" two-bar glyph, set in a tight-tracked bold grotesque at display size, near-black (#191919), straddling the horizontal midline. Behind it, a warm off-white field (#F5F4F1) is covered in hairline gray (#D9D7D1) lines that undulate like distorted graph paper, denser toward the edges and corners and softened by a radial fade so a quiet glow sits behind the type. Monochrome in three inks — field, black wordmark, gray pattern — with no headline, URL, imagery or secondary focal point; the wordmark alone carries the card and the warped mesh is pure texture.

records.name: Epilude Notetaker feature page by Epilude Notetaker
records.description: A near-black, editorial landing page pairs oversized high-contrast serif headlines with restrained sans-serif supporting text and compact pill controls. The hero establishes the product with a large transcript mockup, then the page alternates spacious left/right feature rows over atmospheric landscape imagery; a muted customer-logo panel and integration chips add proof before a darker CTA/footer block closes the page.

records.name: Epilude OG social card — wordmark-only dark canvas by Epilude Notetaker
records.description: A 1200×630 social card that bets everything on a single centered lockup: a near-black canvas with no headline, tagline or product shot. The mark is a run of thin diagonal strokes that gain weight and terminate in a solid block, butted flush against a heavy all-caps italic wordmark in off-white, so the mark reads as acceleration into the name. Two values only — charcoal ground, bone-white type — and roughly 60% empty canvas make it survive being shrunk into a Slack or X preview.

records.name: Eventbrite event discovery homepage by eventbrite.com
records.description: The page opens with a full-bleed concert photo hero whose headline sits on pink-to-purple highlight blocks, with a small pink eyebrow badge and a single white pill CTA — playful but tightly cropped. Below, rhythm shifts from airy (a white rail of outlined category circles) to functional: a location dropdown and underlined filter tabs feed a 4-column event grid where photos, overlay heart/share icons, urgency badges and blue price links carry all the weight while headings stay small. Down the page imagery fades out deliberately: a scrollable destination photo carousel, then three text-only pill-link clusters ('Popular cities', 'Explore by State', nearby cities) that get denser and cheaper to render, before a deep purple 4-column footer. Colour is disciplined: orange only for the logo and search button, blue only for links and active tabs, letting photos provide the vibrancy.

records.name: Eventbrite logo-only Open Graph card by eventbrite.com
records.description: A 1200×630 social card reduced to a single gesture: a flat white canvas with the lowercase "eventbrite" wordmark in warm coral-orange, optically centered and floated slightly above the vertical midpoint. There is no tagline, URL or imagery — the geometric rounded sans, with its tilted "t" ascender and round tittle, does all the recognition work, while roughly 60% negative space keeps the mark crisp even at thumbnail scale. Hierarchy is achieved purely through one saturated hue against one neutral, with no shadows, gradients or borders.

records.name: Fly.io homepage — Computers for agents by fly.io
records.description: The page pairs an old-style serif display face with a sans body and sets nearly everything against soft pastel watercolor gradients — mint, pink, periwinkle and lilac washes — inside large rounded cards that alternate with plain white informational sections. Hierarchy is carried almost entirely by type scale and the purple accent: buttons, stat numerals and links are a single saturated violet against desaturated washes. Whimsical hand-drawn illustrations (a bird-headed computer box, a bed, slugs, a spy) act as spot icons instead of photography, and the page closes with a dark near-black-purple footer containing link columns and a newsletter row.

records.name: Fly.io OG social card — 'Computers for agents' by fly.io
records.description: The card splits its 1200×630 canvas asymmetrically: a quiet left half carries a two-line charcoal serif headline over a soft powder-blue-to-peach sky gradient, while the right half holds a dense hand-drawn cluster of winged, bird-faced servers led by a large purple tower that bleeds off the top and right edges. Wavy ribbon trails in teal, magenta and blue sweep diagonally from the lower left through the illustration, visually stitching the typographic and pictorial halves together and lending a static image a sense of flight. Contrast does the hierarchy work — the darkest element is the type, so it reads first even at thumbnail size — while the pastel palette and textured, bold-outlined illustration give the brand a warm, storybook feel unusual for infrastructure.

records.name: FPLXI fantasy football analytics landing page by fplxi.com
records.description: A data-dense fantasy football analytics landing page set on warm off-white paper, led by a floating black pill nav and a live gameweek ticker. The hero pairs a large serif headline and inline two-step form with a real model leaderboard, so the product's data does the persuading. Down the page the rhythm alternates hairline-bordered white data cards (best XI pitch view, fixtures, position leaders, accuracy charts) with full-black punctuation bands (testimonial, dark stat card), before loosening into pricing with deliberately blurred locked rows and a two-column FAQ accordion. Typography carries the identity: uppercase letterspaced micro-labels, monospaced tabular numerals in every table, and one indigo-blue accent reserved for CTAs and chart bars.

records.name: FPLXI Open Graph social card by fplxi.com
records.description: A 1200×630 social card that splits the canvas into a text column on the left and a floating product mockup collage on the right. The left column stacks the mascot wordmark, a very large two-line headline in near-black, a gray subhead, and three small icon+label feature chips. The right side layers two tilted app screenshots — a hero panel with a mini leaderboard and a player projection card plus a pitch-style "best XI" panel — over soft lavender-to-blue gradient blobs with a faded mascot peeking from the bottom. The palette is almost entirely white, near-black and pastel purple/violet, letting the blue accent bars inside the screenshots be the only saturated hit.

records.name: Framer landing page — AI design agent by framer.com
records.description: A near-black, cinematic product landing page that leads with a short statement headline and an embedded product demo, then alternates generous dark feature sections (each pairing a product screenshot with a small text block and CTA) before settling into a dense bento grid of platform capabilities. Colour is almost entirely black and white with blue/purple gradients reserved for product UI and one accent stat ("99.99% uptime"); full-colour photography only appears in the "Shipped with Framer" gallery, which creates strong rhythm through contrast. Typography is a single rounded geometric sans at very large scale for headings with small, low-contrast supporting copy, and the page ends with a functional chat-style input plus a compact multi-column footer.

records.name: Framer OG social card — site-gallery mosaic with centre logomark by framer.com
records.description: A 1200×630 social card built as a full-bleed mosaic: four-to-five uneven columns of saturated site thumbnails (red, orange, lime, pink, violet) separated by thin black gutters, with edge tiles cropped mid-frame. A black vertical column and horizontal band cross at the centre, forming a plus-shaped field of calm where the white logomark sits as the only focal element — there is no headline at all. The density and colour riot of the gallery does the persuading while the solid-black cross and lone white mark anchor the brand.

records.name: Fresha selfcare booking marketplace landing page by fresha.com
records.description: A consumer booking marketplace that keeps a near-black-on-white editorial base and spends its colour budget in exactly three places: a lavender-to-peach pastel gradient hero, a purple live-booking counter, and yellow review stars. The page runs on rhythm rather than ornament — an airy hero with a segmented pill search bar collapses into three dense, near-identical venue-card carousels, then breathes out again for the app download, testimonial and big-number stats sections, before a business section pairs left-aligned copy with overlapping scheduler/mobile UI mockups. It closes with a deliberately utilitarian country-pill and SEO link grid and a flat grey footer, signalling that the visual theatre lives only where decisions happen.

records.name: Frigade Assist API product landing page by Frigade Assist API
records.description: A bright, engineering-literate SaaS landing page built around a single saturated blue accent on white, with realistic product evidence doing the persuasion: a syntax-highlighted code editor paired with a browser mockup showing a highlighted UI element and a 'STEP 1/3' guide tooltip. Below the hero the page alternates rhythm deliberately — wide centered typographic statements ('Your agent has read your docs…') give way to split proof sections, a full-bleed black-vs-blue comparison panel, a dashed-line system diagram with numbered steps, a version timeline that literally shows docs decaying against a blue Frigade line, and stacked list/log cards. Mono uppercase eyebrows, hairline borders, soft floating shadows on mockups and grayscale logo clouds keep it technical and credible, before a rounded royal-blue CTA panel and a dense multi-column footer close the page.

records.name: Frigade Assist API social card by Frigade Assist API
records.description: A 1200×630 social card uses a near-black charcoal canvas with subtle vertical panels and diagonal texture at the edges. The white wordmark sits centered above a large two-line headline, while a thin electric-blue glowing arc and small white pointer create a visual divider; the final phrase is isolated in bright blue for emphasis.

records.name: Incredible fintech waitlist landing page by getincredible.com
records.description: A sparse pre-launch landing page built around one oversized rounded hero card with a lime-to-cream gradient, huge tightly-set black headline, and a small pill tag plus black CTA. Below the card the page drops to near-empty white space with a single download CTA and dense fine-print legal text, creating a stark contrast between one bold statement and regulatory small print.

records.name: Gojo landing page — notch utility suite by Gojo
records.description: A calm, utility-led product page... Analysis below in description.

records.name: Gojo social card by Gojo
records.description: A 1200×630 social card uses a heavily blurred, warm-toned background image as an atmospheric full-bleed canvas, with amber, rust, olive and charcoal areas blending into one another. The focal stack is centered: a white abstract mark sits above a large rounded wordmark, followed by a smaller one-line tagline; generous vertical spacing and strong white contrast keep the hierarchy legible over the soft imagery.

records.name: Goodreads logged-out homepage by goodreads.com
records.description: A warm, link-dense community homepage that saves all its colour for one moment: a saturated orange-to-yellow hero band with flat-illustrated readers flanking a large serif headline. A white signup card overlaps the hero's right edge, then the page settles onto a cream paper background and alternates editorial text blocks, book-cover discovery panels and a scannable right rail of news, lists and CTAs. Hierarchy is carried by a serif display face against small sans-serif body text, with dark teal reserved exclusively for navigational links, so even the dense genre and awards directories feel calm and consistent.

records.name: Goodreads Open Graph social card by goodreads.com
records.description: A restrained 1200×630 social card built from three flat colours and one curved edge. A plum field fills roughly 85% of the canvas beneath a cream band, and its top edge rises, dips to a point at dead centre and rises again — a subtle nod to the valley of an open book. The headline is set in a warm, high-contrast serif at display scale with a single italic word for emphasis, and the lowercase wordmark repeats beneath it in amber at about half the size. No photography, gradients or product UI; all of the visual interest comes from the organic curve, the colour block and typographic scale.

records.name: Granola landing page by granola.ai
records.description: An editorial landing page built on a cream ground (#FAF8F1) with a large serif display face doing almost all the persuasive work — headlines run to full-viewport width ('For the doers', 'Works everywhere you do'). The page alternates rhythm deliberately: light hero and hairline-divided feature rows, then a giant type statement, a near-black logo band, a chartreuse chat band, dark testimonial cards, and back to light. Every product claim is evidenced by a macOS-style window mockup with cream notepad UI, often composited over landscape photography. It closes with a multi-column footer that dissolves into an enormous full-bleed wordmark.

records.name: Granola AI social card by granola.ai
records.description: A 1200×630 social card uses a vivid, tactile collage background—lime graphic paper at left and a pink-blue woven textile at right—as a frame for a large warm-white rounded browser-like panel. Inside, a bold black wordmark sits above an oversized high-contrast serif headline arranged in four lines, creating a clear focal hierarchy; small browser dots and a compact utility badge add interface cues without competing with the typography.

records.name: Hinge corporate homepage by hinge.co
records.description: A warm editorial corporate page built on a cream canvas where tiny plum eyebrow labels sit above oversized serif headlines in asymmetric two-column compositions. Rhythm comes from alternating bands — cream editorial sections, a near-black testimonial band with a slider, a cream careers section with a photo strip bleeding off the right edge, then a merged dark press band and footer. Documentary-style candid photography, pill buttons, and hand-drawn oval-and-arrow annotations in aubergine give it a human, print-magazine quality rather than a product-marketing feel.

records.name: Hob agent workspace landing page by hob
records.description: A very light, spacious product page uses oversized black sans-serif headlines, restrained gray body copy, thin dividers, and softly bordered interface mockups to establish a calm professional tone. The page moves from a centered hero and large app screenshot into alternating screenshot-led feature sections, a dense practical feature grid, testimonials, FAQ rows, and a compact orange CTA before ending with a quiet multi-column footer.

records.name: hob agent workspace OG social card by hob
records.description: A disciplined two-zone composition at 1200×630: a centered three-line headline in a heavy white grotesque occupies the top half on near-black, while a cropped dark app window rises from the bottom edge and provides the product proof. All colour weight is deliberately withheld — the canvas is black/white/gray until the small circular white badge with a teal-to-orange bar mark, which does double duty as wordmark and focal accent. The window is rendered as atmosphere (low-contrast UI chrome, readable diff colours but illegible body text) so the headline and badge stay the only fully legible elements even at feed thumbnail size.

records.name: Hugging Face homepage by huggingface.co
records.description: A white page anchored by two near-black rounded cards — the hero with a live product screenshot bleeding off its right edge, and the Team & Enterprise band mid-page with floating 3D shapes — bookending airy centered sections. Density alternates deliberately: dense three-column trending lists with tiny stat metadata, a bento grid of feature cards embedding real UI mocks (activity feed, code snippet, modality grid, profile), then an airy masonry of open-source library cards carrying star counts as social proof. The yellow mascot is the only saturated accent on an otherwise black/white/gray system, reappearing as a full emoji pile above the footer to close the page playfully.

records.name: Hugging Face OG social card by huggingface.co
records.description: A 1200×630 share card built around a single focal row: a die-cut sticker mascot on the left balanced by a two-line, extra-bold near-black headline on the right, the whole group vertically and horizontally centered on a white canvas with a barely-there grey gradient toward the bottom. Hierarchy comes entirely from scale and weight contrast — roughly 90px headline type against the ~200px mark — with the sticker's white outline and soft shadow giving the mark lift off the flat background. All margins are generous (top and bottom quarters are pure whitespace), so the card stays legible at thumbnail size in Slack or X previews.

records.name: Inngest landing page — 'Unbreakable Agents, Invisible Infra' by inngest.com
records.description: A near-black developer landing page that leads with typography: an enormous uppercase grotesque headline whose second line drops to outline-only stroke, while floating mono code-callout chips (step.run(), step.waitForEvent()) drift through a particle field. Below the hero the page alternates airy statement sections with dense utilitarian grids — three feature cards with one coral-gradient active tab, a 3×2 durability-primitive grid, a 2×3 use-case grid — all separated by hairline borders on barely-raised panels, with a single coral accent doing all the colour work. The rhythm then shifts through proof (grayscale logo strip, portrait testimonial carousel), explanation (before/after architecture diagram, numbered SDK-step carousel), and trust (throughput line chart, CISO compliance grid), closing with three template quickstart cards and a multi-column footer.

records.name: Inngest OG social card by inngest.com
records.description: A 1200×630 social card built on a single saturated orange field with a fine grain overlay that keeps the flat colour from feeling sterile. The logo lockup sits top-left and a left-aligned two-line headline owns the middle of the frame: the first line is solid white bold sans, the second line repeats at identical size but in hollow outline type — hierarchy achieved through fill treatment rather than scale or a second colour. The bottom third is deliberately empty, letting the type, colour and texture do all the work.

records.name: Jackalope landing page by Jackalope
