records.description: A soft, friendly landing page built on a near-white lavender background with an electric indigo accent used sparingly for CTAs and highlighted words. Hierarchy comes from very large two-tone display headlines (black first phrase, indigo second), then the page breaks into bento-style feature cards whose tops are pastel-tinted illustration panels (lavender, mint, cream, blush) with white text halves below. Rhythm alternates between card grids, an icon-led two-column feature list with hairline dividers, a tabbed walkthrough with a large purple canvas illustration, a UI screenshot showcase, a theme switcher demo, and a two-column accordion FAQ. A saturated indigo footer with a giant wordmark and an email-capture form closes the page. Density stays low; generous whitespace and consistent card radius/soft shadows carry the cohesive, approachable feel.

records.name: Jackalope “Many agents. One workspace.” OG social card by Jackalope
records.description: A 1200×630 social card split into a light brand half and a dark product half on a warm off-white field. Nine outlined rabbit silhouettes shift hue from orange through violet to blue before resolving into one solid black jackalope — a literal “many → one” story — while thin orange and blue circuit traces with node dots thread across the canvas. The two-line statement (“Many agents.” in ink, “One workspace.” in orange) anchors the bottom-left above a monospace domain, and a dark tasks-board screenshot, tilted a few degrees and bleeding off the right and bottom edges, supplies the dense UI contrast that makes the flat left half read instantly at feed size.

records.name: Kinetics — spring physics animation library by kinetics.colorion.co
records.description: A near-black catalogue of 111 spring-driven interface effects organised as three dense demo grids — Interaction & Input, Feedback & State, Surface & Motion — each introduced by a letterspaced uppercase header with a monospace counter. The hero buys contrast through sparseness: an animated spring waveform, a huge condensed uppercase headline where one word flips to saturated orange, and a floating card previewing the CSS/React/AI-prompt handoff. Below, every card repeats one disciplined template (demo stage → monospace physics parameters → name → one-line description → View code link), so the single orange accent and the monospace meta layer carry the whole identity.

records.name: Kinetics motion library OG card by kinetics.colorion.co
records.description: A 1200×630 near-black social card organised into three horizontal bands: a small top-left lockup (orange dot plus bold monospace wordmark), an oversized two-line display headline in extra-bold type where only the final word "weight." flips to orange, and a damped spring curve that enters at full amplitude behind the headline and decays to a settled flat hairline ending in a solid orange dot. A monospace keyword strip in muted gray with middot separators anchors the bottom margin. Colour is restricted to off-white, orange and gray on black, and the pairing of a heavy humanist display face with monospace secondary text gives the whole card a precise, engineering-flavoured tone — the curve literally demonstrates the product's pitch.

records.name: Krea AI homepage — dark generative-media app landing by krea.ai
records.description: A dark, app-style landing page where a permanent left sidebar (pinned white Sign-in pill, grouped tool list with colourful mini-icons) frames a starfield hero whose centrepiece is a conversational prompt bar rather than a traditional CTA. Below, the rhythm changes section by section: a full-width announcement banner, a dense bento of small feature tiles beside one large promo card, horizontally scrolled template and video-model cards with Featured/New pills and credit costs, then a quiet centred model gallery with search and tabs, and finally a dense multi-column sitemap footer. Hierarchy is carried by a few large light display headlines set against otherwise 12–13px utilitarian text, hairline borders and #141414 panels, with a single blue accent reserved for primary actions while media thumbnails supply the colour.

records.name: Winszn Labs studio landing page by labs.winszn.xyz
records.description: A dark, brutalist landing page for an engineering studio that earns trust through evidence rather than polish claims. The hero pairs a huge tight-tracked headline and 3D "keyboard" illustration with two stat cards (one vivid orange, one black), then an orange full-bleed band of tech-stack pill badges transitions into a near-black case-study grid. Each project card is a real product screenshot plus a factual "evidence line" and tag chips — density stays high and the rhythm alternates between image cards and typographic stat cards. The lower half shifts to a services bento with 3D icons, a numbered five-step process list, a manifesto section, and closes with an orange contact panel containing the enquiry form, a meta footer, and an oversized cropped wordmark. Orange (#E8500A-ish) is used sparingly but with total confidence against near-black surfaces and mono-spaced micro-labels.

records.name: winszn labs — dark Swiss OG card with orange slab by labs.winszn.xyz
records.description: A near-black 1200×630 card built on Swiss poster grammar: a tracked uppercase wordmark lockup top-left, a huge white grotesque headline left-of-centre as the single focal point, and a flat orange slab bleeding off the top-right edge with a tonal near-black square overlapping it for depth without any shadow or gradient. A thin hairline rule separates a quiet footer of letterspaced micro-labels, including literal hex swatches (#EB4604, #99A57D) printed as content — a self-referential designer's footnote. Hierarchy comes almost entirely from type scale (roughly 6:1 between headline and labels) and one hot accent against monochrome ground.

records.name: Ledger — hardware wallets homepage by ledger.com
records.description: A full-black landing page where pure black fields dominate and only small controlled accents (orange primary buttons, purple gradients behind product shots, colourful crypto logos) carry energy. The hero pairs a compact headline block with a large gradient product render, followed immediately by a slim trust-stat strip. Rhythm alternates between wide cinematic full-width banners (the 'Bitcoin 3D' router banner, the cashback banner), bordered 4-up product comparison cards with corner tick marks, a sparse crypto-logo strip, and text-led sections with generous whitespace. Type scale is steep: very large white section headlines over small gray body copy. The page closes with a testimonial carousel, a two-column FAQ accordion, a huge centered closing statement in purple gradient, and a dense multi-column footer.

records.name: Ledger OG social card — fanned hardware wallets on dark gradient by ledger.com
records.description: A 1200×630 social card built on a near-black radial gradient that lightens toward the upper left, giving the product photography a studio backdrop. The [ LEDGER ] wordmark sits alone in the top ~15%, its corner-bracket motif doubling as a frame device, while three hardware wallets fan across the lower two-thirds at slightly different rotations, bleeding off the bottom edge for scale. Each device screen carries real, legible UI (a Bitcoin signing prompt, a send/receive summary, an app grid) so the card communicates function, not just hardware, with a single orange accent on the centre device acting as the only saturated colour and focal anchor.

records.name: Lemonade insurance landing page by lemonade.com
records.description: A single-accent, centered composition: a serif display headline sits over a panorama of grayscale hand-drawn line illustrations, and one hot pink (~#FF0083) carries every CTA, star, inline highlight and the single filled illustration element. The page moves down in alternating white and pale-gray bands — bundle-pricing cards with checkboxes, oversized pink stars above tweet-style testimonial cards, annotated phone mockups, a soft-gray bubble chart of switcher stats, an illustrated donut explainer and three stamp-like trust badges — before a dense black multi-column footer with long legal fine print. Hierarchy comes almost entirely from a strict two-typeface scale and the scarcity of the accent, which keeps a chatty consumer story readable.

records.name: Lemonade OG social card — 'Forget Everything You Know About Insurance' by lemonade.com
records.description: A 1200×630 social card split roughly in half: the left column stacks a script wordmark above a three-line serif headline, while the right half is occupied by a single monochrome line-art scene (house, bench, person, dog) that bleeds to the canvas edges. The palette is strictly greyscale — charcoal type on white, illustration strokes and flat fills in light grey — with a thin light-grey band along the bottom acting as a ground line that the illustration's shadows sit on. Hierarchy is handled purely by scale and weight contrast: the oversized serif headline reads first, the friendly script logo second, the illustration third, all without a single accent colour.

records.name: Linear landing page by linear.app
records.description: A near-black canvas with almost no colour until two saturated testimonial cards (lavender gradient and chartreuse) break the monochrome near the end. Hierarchy is built from an oversized tight-tracked grotesque headline, small-caps meta labels, and dense product mockups that carry all the visual complexity; separation comes from hairline borders and faint glows rather than shadows. The page runs a strict repeating template below the hero — left-aligned two-line heading, right-column paragraph, full-width UI composite, then a four-column 'Features' index — which creates rhythm while the changelog columns and testimonial duo change the pacing before a centered CTA and a five-column footer.

records.name: Linear social card — minimal wordmark lockup on dark gradient by linear.app
records.description: A 1200×630 social card that is essentially pure brand: a single centered lockup of a white circular mark with diagonal slits next to a bold white wordmark, floating on a near-black canvas that lightens into a soft grey glow toward the bottom. No headline, tagline or imagery — the restraint and the ambient vertical gradient do all the work, making the logo read instantly at small share sizes.

records.name: Live Captions social share card by Live Captions by Subanana
records.description: A 1200×630 share card built like a sticker sheet: a warm amber canvas with large organic blob shapes, a left column carrying a die-cut logo badge, a three-line heavy headline outlined in white, and a yellow CTA pill. The right two-thirds is a hand-tilted collage of four pastel mini product surfaces — lavender, cream, pink and mint — each packed with one realistic detail such as a live caption with a blinking cursor, a captioned video frame, meeting notes and a transcript search. Thick white sticker borders, varied rotations and soft shadows unify the collage so the card still reads at chat-thumbnail size.

records.name: Liveblocks landing page by liveblocks.io
records.description: A near-black developer landing page where hierarchy is carried almost entirely by type scale and luminance rather than colour. The top edge fades from a faint blue-violet glow into solid black, framing a tight 72px nav and a centred hero: a pill-shaped announcement badge, a two-line display headline at roughly 64-72px, a muted grey subheadline, then a single white pill CTA beside a quiet text link. Density stays extremely low and spacing generous until a blurred product visual begins to emerge from the black below, hinting at the demo without breaking the monochrome mood.

records.name: Liveblocks OG social card by liveblocks.io
records.description: A 1200×630 social card built on a near-black canvas with a faint photographic grain and corner vignette, letting a single two-line white grotesque headline carry the entire composition at ~90px. The product concept is enacted rather than illustrated: two collaboration cursor chips — a magenta '✨ AI' tag and a lavender 'Stacy' name tag with cursor arrows — overlap the headline edges at opposite corners, bringing the only colour on the card. A small centred wordmark at the bottom closes the vertical axis, so hierarchy reads headline → cursor accents → brand in one glance.

records.name: Loom video messaging homepage by loom.com
records.description: A spacious, white landing page uses oversized black headings, compact supporting copy, and bright blue pill CTAs to establish a clear, friendly hierarchy. The page develops from a cinematic rounded video hero into social proof, alternating product-feature rows, pastel use-case cards, compact feature lists, blue editorial panels, dark security and enterprise sections, a testimonial carousel, and a broad pale-blue link-heavy footer. Rounded containers, soft shadows, blue accents, and pastel product imagery keep the long page cohesive while the rhythm shifts between open editorial whitespace and denser utility sections.

records.name: Loom Social Card by loom.com
records.description: This social card splits the canvas in two: a solid black left half that carries the wordmark at the top, a bold white headline in the middle, and a quiet URL lockup at the bottom, and a light right half that shows a product video frame with teal UI accents. The 50/50 split creates instant readability at thumbnail size, while the asymmetric placement of the headline keeps the text block feeling editorial rather than boxed. Colour is used sparingly — black, white, and a single teal accent — so the card reads clearly even at very small share sizes.

records.name: Loqua — AI voice dictation landing page by Loqua
records.description: A long editorial landing page on a warm cream base with a lime/olive accent, built around generous serif display headlines that alternate with compact sans body copy. The rhythm alternates dramatically: cream feature sections with side-by-side text and demo panels, then a full-bleed black band for the app-compatibility grid and again for a dense testimonial wall, so the page breathes in light/dark cycles. Playful touches — sticker badges, small illustrations, a sticky Product Hunt card and "Try it now" interactive demo — keep the restrained layout from feeling corporate.

records.name: Loqua icon-only OG card by Loqua
records.description: An icon-only social card that commits to a single focal point: a flat teal field (~#00A78F) carrying one white rounded-square tile near centre, which holds a near-black mark of three tapered vertical bars that read simultaneously as a letterform and a voice waveform. There is no headline, wordmark or URL — hierarchy comes entirely from scale (the tile spans roughly 45% of the canvas height) and the saturated field against the white tile. The very large squircle radius on both tile and mark terminals keeps every edge soft, so the composition stays unmistakable even at thumbnail size.

records.name: Lorikeet AI customer concierge landing page by lorikeetcx.ai
records.description: A cream-canvas landing page that pairs a large editorial serif with small airy sans copy and recurring black pill CTAs. Proof is carried by an asymmetric bento — photo-quote testimonial cards and stat cards whose oversized serif numerals (97%, 60%, 99%) sit on mint, sky and butter gradient washes — followed by a two-row monochrome logo wall. Below the hero the rhythm loosens: a failure-vs-success comparison with embedded grey and mint UI mockups plus a gradient scenario progress bar, then airy centred statement sections (channel icons, a glowing app tile ringed by workflow chips, a curved magenta-to-orange integration diagram, a single voice-resolution card), a three-card stories carousel, an oversized serif closer, and a footer that blooms into a blurred magenta-green gradient field.

records.name: Lorikeet AI customer-experience social card by lorikeetcx.ai
records.description: A 1200×630 social card built as a collage: a bold serif wordmark sits top-centre above one large rounded hero photo, while four lifestyle photos bleed off the canvas corners and five frosted notification pills float between them. The bottom half erupts in blurred vertical light rays — magenta on the left, violet in the middle, amber on the right — that fade upward into the white canvas. Hierarchy is driven by scale and position (centre photo > wordmark > pills > cropped corners), and the playful gradient energy is grounded by the disciplined white space at the top.

records.name: Lovable landing page by lovable.dev
records.description: The page runs on a warm cream base with near-black type and one signature asset: a blue-to-magenta aurora gradient that opens the hero, reappears as glows inside the dark showcase, and closes the page as a footer band. The hero is prompt-first — a ~64px headline over a large white rounded chat input that recurs verbatim as the final CTA, framing the product as a conversation. Below, rhythm alternates light and dark: three hairline-bordered cards, then an inset near-black container holding five feature panels (each a small bold sub-head plus a large glowing gradient visual), a logo wall, a side-peek testimonial carousel with a metrics column, and finally a stack of oversized stat numbers over a rising gradient area chart before a dense five-column footer.

records.name: Luma events landing page by lu.ma
records.description: A single centred column on pure white, led by a display headline whose final line is the page's only loud accent — a pink-to-orange gradient — hovering above a black pill CTA with a soft glow. The page then alternates density: a six-card popular-events row with poster thumbnails and grey metadata, a two-row community grid of icon-chip cards, and a 12-tile category grid where tiny single-pastel line icons carry all the colour. Everything stays flat (1px warm-grey borders, 8–12px radii, no shadows), section headings shrink to small bold left-aligned labels, and the page closes by mirroring the hero — a two-line gradient statement with paired pill buttons — over a hairline footer.

records.name: Luma gradient social card by lu.ma
records.description: A 1200×630 social card built almost entirely from atmosphere: a heavily blurred mesh gradient where hot pink dominates the centre, coral-orange pools in the lower right, a sky-blue patch enters at the top-left corner and luminous white breaks glow through the upper right. The only focal element is a white lowercase wordmark, slightly left of true centre, closed by a small four-point sparkle that acts as the brand's punctuation mark. With no headline, CTA or imagery, hierarchy is achieved purely through white-on-saturated-pastel contrast, which keeps the card legible even when shrunk to a small link preview.

records.name: Daedalus studio landing page by madebydaedalus.com
records.description: A two-person software studio site built on a warm cream canvas with hairline rules and an alternating band rhythm: cream hero, cream studio intro, near-black craft section, cream project list, lilac contact band. Hierarchy is carried almost entirely by an enormous tight-tracking grotesque display face against small grey body text, with colour used only as punctuation — a gradient underline, a lilac word, a purple question mark. The playful layer (eyed mascot, pixel sprites, tilted letter stickers, hand-drawn arrow) sits against a rigorously ordered grid, and the dark band proves the studio's 'software that feels good' claim with three genuinely interactive widgets: a London clock, a weather card with hourly forecast, and a playable audio tile.

records.name: MasterClass education landing page by masterclass.com
records.description: A fully dark education landing page that treats cinematic instructor photography and video stills as the entire visual system, set on near-black surfaces so the imagery glows. Type runs on three voices — an ultra-condensed uppercase display for campaign statements, a neutral bold sans for UI and section headers, and a high-contrast serif reserved for class titles — while a single crimson CTA repeats down the page and one chartreuse accent marks the certificates cross-sell. Rhythm alternates dense utility sections (onboarding quiz, icon benefit list, FAQ accordions) with sparse full-bleed cinematic spotlights and paired carousels, keeping conversion CTAs visible at every register change.

records.name: Mastra Factory — agent-powered software delivery landing page by Mastra Factory
records.description: A near-black developer landing page that argues with rendered product artefacts rather than adjectives: after a ring-motif hero it shows an in-page four-column kanban of agent-processed issues, then a monospace-labelled six-stage pipeline stepper. Hierarchy is built almost entirely from type scale and grey value, with colour rationed to meaning — one orange ribbon announcement, a green glow on the recommended plan, a blue tint on enterprise, a violet pill for the active stage. Rhythm alternates airy centred blocks (hero, final CTA) with dense rounded panels (board, stepper, pricing, case studies, FAQ, footer), closing by repeating the hero's exact CTA pair.

records.name: Mastra Factory OG social card by Mastra Factory
records.description: A stark monochrome 1200×630 social card. The mastra wordmark with its dotted molecule-like mark sits top-left, while the page title "Factory" is set large and bold on the lower-left baseline, leaving the right two-thirds and the middle band entirely as empty black negative space. The tension between the two corner-anchored text blocks and the vast emptiness gives the card its confidence; no illustration, gradient or imagery competes with the type.

records.name: Meetup homepage — social events discovery landing by meetup.com
records.description: A consumer social landing built around repeating event-card grids set against airy, illustrated interludes. Warm candid photography is masked into organic blobs with handwritten labels and doodles, while the functional layers — dual search bar, card grids, category tiles, city tiles — stay disciplined: white canvas, near-black type, charcoal pill CTAs, hot-pink brand accent and purple text links. Rhythm alternates dense four-column card sections with wide-spaced centered panels (join CTA, how-it-works, editorial strip), ending in a dark rounded footer with four link columns and app badges.

records.name: Meetup OG social card — 'The people platform' by meetup.com
records.description: A 1200×630 social card built almost entirely from typography and negative space: a small black wordmark sits top-left, then a three-line stacked headline ('The / people / platform.') set in an ultra-heavy grotesque with tight leading, left-aligned and pushed to the lower two-thirds of the canvas. The type is punctuated by three hand-drawn watercolor icons inline with the words — an orange compass disc, a purple pair-of-people glyph and a pink heart — which supply the only colour and make the sentence feel spoken rather than stated. The entire right third stays empty, so the composition reads instantly at thumbnail size while still feeling handcrafted.

records.name: Mercury fintech banking landing page by mercury.com
records.description: A long dark-mode landing page that alternates between dense product-proof sections and airy, emotionally toned statements, giving the scroll a deliberate rhythm. Deep navy-black grounds everything; a serif display face carries the big statements while a grotesque sans handles UI, body and the extensive legal footnotes. Product UI screenshots and photography anchor the proof sections, while cream-tinted abstract 3D renders (spheres, cones, fingerprint, toggle) carry the brand-feel sections, all wrapped in hairline-bordered rounded cards with a single blue accent reserved for primary CTAs.

records.name: Mintlify marketing homepage by mintlify.com
records.description: The page runs on a warm cream canvas with hairline-bordered bento cards and a signature mixed-type headline that pairs a transitional serif with a neutral sans, the second line dropped to grey. Rhythm alternates deliberately down the page: a dense live-metrics ticker with green tabular numerals, an airy feature bento, full-bleed tinted customer-story carousels with oversized stats, a calm 2×3 testimonial grid, then editorial blog cards. Thin gradient thread-lines sweep behind the hero, the scale section, and the pre-footer CTA, tying the whole page together without competing with the black-and-green type system.

records.name: Mintlify Open Graph social card by mintlify.com
records.description: A 1200×630 brand card built on a near-black canvas with a single centered lockup: a green gradient leaf mark beside a white lowercase geometric wordmark. Depth comes from faint oversized circle outlines and diagonal strokes sitting a few percent above the background, forming an abstract line grid that never competes with the wordmark. The restraint is the point — no headline, URL or tagline, just one confident focal point with generous empty space on all sides.

records.name: Mistral AI enterprise AI platform landing page by mistral.ai
records.description: A restrained, grid-led enterprise AI landing page pairs oversized black typography with thin rules, generous white space, and bright pixel-art panels in orange, red, blue, and yellow. The page expands from a compact hero and customer-news carousel into a dense product capability map, then alternates structured service cards with darker deployment options, a vivid orange CTA, and a highly organized multi-column footer.

records.name: Mistral AI Open Graph social card by mistral.ai
records.description: A 1200×630 social card split into two horizontal halves: a quiet white upper field carrying a two-line black grotesque headline flush left and the pixel-gradient wordmark anchored right, and a lower field built from flat horizontal colour bands stepping from orange through red-orange to deep crimson. A tiny pixel-art black cat sits on the left of the red band as a mascot easter egg, and faint bezier guide lines with anchor points are traced in the bands' right side as a subtle drafting motif. Everything is flat — no shadows, photos or gradients outside the logo — so the palette and the scale contrast between headline and bands carry the whole composition.

records.name: mmbl.io voice-to-task app landing page by mmbl.io
records.description: A dark, type-led landing page for a voice-capture task app, built on a near-black canvas with a single lavender editorial interstitial that resets the rhythm mid-page. Every section repeats a disciplined pattern: a two-line display headline (second line knocked back to gray or accented in periwinkle), a small right-aligned supporting paragraph, then a media moment — a tilted phone mockup wrapped in organic colour blobs, a side-by-side capture/parse demo, or a mockup paired with stacked feature blocks. Density stays low with generous whitespace; colour is rationed to small doses (waveform bars, pill tags, glyphs) against #0b0c10 panels, slightly lighter cards, and pill-shaped buttons with soft radii and no decorative shadows. The colourful waveform mark is the only recurring graphic motif, tying voice capture to brand identity down to the footer.

records.name: Mock Magic device mockup generator landing page by Mock Magic: Video Presets
records.description: A near-monochrome dark landing page where all colour is quarantined inside product imagery — painterly phone screens and a warm orange editor capture pop against a black canvas. Hierarchy is carried almost entirely by type weight and a strict white-on-black/gray body split; the only chromatic UI elements are green check icons in pricing. Rhythm alternates between split layouts (hero text + cropped device), a full-bleed light-mode app screenshot that inverts the palette for contrast, a three-column feature row, a centred FAQ accordion, twin pricing cards with dimmed locked features, and a dense SEO footer with newsletter capture. Buttons are the inverse of the theme — white fills with black text — so a single CTA style repeats from navbar to footer.

records.name: Mock Magic OG social card by Mock Magic: Video Presets
records.description: A 1200×630 social card split into two asymmetric zones: a quiet black left half carrying the wordmark and a two-line white headline, and a dense right half where a laptop, phone and watch stack bleed off the edges. All three screens show the same blue-and-orange painterly artwork, so the product's value (your content on every device) is demonstrated without a single word of explanation. Colour is withheld everywhere except inside the screens, which makes the artwork the only chromatic event and gives the card its pop.

records.name: Modeinspect AI-native design platform landing page by Modeinspect
records.description: A long-form product landing page alternates a warm off-white canvas with near-black sections, using a luminous lime green as the only strong accent. Oversized sans-serif headlines are paired with occasional distressed or pixel-like display lettering, while the rhythm moves from a spacious hero and product mockup into denser feature grids, proof cards, workflow comparisons, FAQ rows, and a high-contrast closing CTA.

records.name: Modeinspect OG social card by Modeinspect
records.description: A typography-only social card at roughly 1200×630 built on a single centered axis. A soft vertical gradient — pale lime at the top fading to muted lavender-taupe at the bottom — carries a three-line headline in deep indigo, set very large in a geometric grotesque with tight leading, with the word 'code' swapped into a chunky pixel-style face as the conceptual punchline. The only other element is a small bottom-centered lockup of a cursor glyph with a lime sparkle behind it beside the wordmark, so the headline does all the communicating and the brand stays a quiet footnote.

records.name: Moji — Markdown reader landing page by Moji
records.description: A desktop-app landing page built on an editorial, Japanese-inflected design language: large serif headlines, seal-stamp kanji badges sectioning the page, and a warm paper-beige base that alternates with near-black sections for rhythm. Product proof comes from dark app-window screenshots with small floating labels, and the palette is almost entirely monochrome with a single crimson accent reserved for underlines, seal stamps and CTAs. Density stays low — one idea per band — until the download section compresses into three platform cards.

records.name: Moji Open Graph social card by Moji
records.description: A 1200×630 share card split into two zones: a paper-white identity column on the left and a tilted dark-mode app screenshot floating over a sumi-e ink-wash texture on the right. Hierarchy on the left runs brush-drawn mark → red seal stamp → high-contrast serif wordmark → letterspaced caps tagline with one red keyword → a hairline-divided four-icon feature row → repo URL, all locked to a single left margin. The palette is strictly paper white, ink black and seal red (the stamp motif repeats top-left and bottom-right), so the dark UI panel carries all the contrast weight and the card reads instantly at thumbnail size.

records.name: Monarch personal finance landing page by monarchmoney.com
records.description: A long-form fintech landing page pairs large editorial serif headlines with restrained sans-serif body copy and a mostly warm-white canvas. The hero uses a lifestyle video/image backdrop, translucent data overlays, and a floating white CTA card; below it, the rhythm shifts through credibility logos, centered product explanation, a feature grid, alternating screenshot-and-copy rows, testimonials, press proof, community resources, pricing, and a high-contrast orange closing CTA. Orange is reserved for promotion bars, labels, buttons, progress accents, and the final conversion block, while product screenshots and lightly bordered cards provide most of the visual detail.

records.name: Monarch financial dashboard social card by monarchmoney.com
records.description: A 1200×630 social card uses a warm off-white canvas with the Monarch wordmark centered near the top, leaving the lower two-thirds for a large desktop finance dashboard mockup and an overlapping smartphone. The focal hierarchy moves from the restrained black-and-orange wordmark to the dense product preview; rounded device frames, fine gray UI text, and colorful cash-flow bands provide detail without changing the clean editorial composition.

records.name: Monzo consumer banking homepage by monzo.com
records.description: A long consumer bank homepage built almost entirely from rounded slabs and cards that alternate between white, warm grey, hot coral and deep navy, creating a strong colour rhythm as you scroll. The hero pairs warm lifestyle photography with a short bold headline, then the page moves through carousel-based feature rows, a bento grid of support tiles, a sign-up stepper, and finally unusually transparent survey-ranking tables drawn with coral bars. Pill buttons, 16–24px radii, phone mockups and tiny regulatory small print give it a friendly but credible financial tone.

records.name: Neon cloud database platform landing page by neon.tech
records.description: A high-contrast infrastructure landing page uses near-black surfaces, oversized white typography, muted gray supporting copy, and electric green accents to create a technical but editorial tone. The page moves from a dense hero with navigation, abstract database imagery, capability tiles, and customer logos into spacious feature demonstrations; pale mint interludes reset the rhythm before returning to black sections for branching, authentication, enterprise features, proof points, a final CTA, and a compact multi-column footer.

records.name: Neon social preview card by neon.tech
records.description: A 1200630 OG card on a near-black canvas with abstract vertical neon bars in green, teal and amber glowing across the top two-thirds, like data streams or an equalizer. The logo lockup sits top-left, a small red kicker line ('A Databricks company') with a tiny icon sits above a two-line white headline in a clean sans, bottom-left aligned. The composition is asymmetric and calm: bright abstract texture upper-right, quiet dark space lower-left for the type.

records.name: Neopress AI website builder landing page by Neopress
records.description: A long-form editorial landing page uses oversized high-contrast serif headlines with restrained sans-serif body copy and generous white space. The hero establishes the product through a large browser mockup, then the page alternates between template galleries, service cards, founder-led editorial content, product workflows, SEO explanations, tool grids, and pricing; soft beige sections and pastel image backdrops create rhythm without adding saturated brand colour. Thin gray borders, mostly square cards, minimal shadows, and black CTA buttons keep the interface precise while the increasingly information-dense lower sections communicate product depth.

records.name: Neopress Open Graph brand card by Neopress
records.description: A maximum-restraint social card: a warm cream canvas (roughly #FAF7F0, deliberately not pure white) with a single black lockup dead-centre on both axes. The lockup pairs a thick geometric mark — a rounded-diamond outline whose stroke pinches at the four vertices around a white core — with 'Neopress' set in a bold, high-contrast editorial serif with tight tracking; the icon's height is matched to the cap height so the two read as one unit occupying about a third of the canvas width. There is no headline, URL or imagery: hierarchy, scale contrast (huge ink shapes vs ~25% margins of empty paper) and the serif-on-paper tone do all the work. A stray red pixel in the top-left corner reads as a capture artefact rather than part of the design.

records.name: Noodle Seed AI agent platform landing page by Noodle Seed
records.description: A long-form, near-black AI platform landing page uses oversized lightweight white typography, restrained gray copy, and thin dividers to create a calm technical rhythm. The hero is sparse and centered, then the page alternates between proof points, product demos, warm ambient-gradient feature panels, architecture diagrams, dense numbered security content, FAQ rows, and a compact CTA/footer; orange-gold glow is reserved for buttons, runtime imagery, and subtle background atmosphere.

records.name: Noodle Seed OG social card by Noodle Seed
records.description: A 1200×630 social card on a near-black canvas, with a dramatic plume of orange-to-red light streaks curving up from the bottom edges like wings, framing a fully centered text block. Hierarchy is strict: small wordmark with a leaf/seed glyph, then a two-line headline in large white rounded sans, then a two-line muted gray subhead. The dark void in the middle gives the copy total legibility while the warm swirls supply all the colour and energy.

records.name: Notion homepage — hero with product collage by notion.com
records.description: The page opens with an enormous, tightly-tracked two-line headline where one word sits in a pale-blue highlight pill, then immediately drops into a layered collage of real product mockups with hand-drawn ink doodles peeking over the edges. Rhythm below alternates between airy left-aligned statement headlines and dense UI cards: a two-up feature grid with live mockups, a five-card use-case row, then duotone photo testimonials washed in saturated red, blue and amber. A grey logo wall, an icon-led stats marquee, a beige CTA band and a quote-bearing footer close the page; Notion blue is the only strong accent against an otherwise black-on-white editorial system.

records.name: Teams and agents social card by notion.com
records.description: A 1200×630 white social card uses a centered vertical composition: a small black wordmark anchors the top, followed by an oversized two-line headline with a pale-blue rounded highlight around one phrase. A row of colorful illustrated circular avatars creates the visual bridge into a cropped grayscale product-interface image along the bottom, balancing stark black typography with playful accents and a light editorial rhythm.

records.name: Obsidian marketing homepage by obsidian.md
records.description: A near-black page carried almost entirely by product vignettes: the hero, the bento grid, the sync card and the docs mock are all real-looking UI built in DOM, so the app itself is the imagery. Hierarchy comes from a strict type scale (oversized headline with terminal period → 40px section heads → 15px gray body) and hairline rgba-white borders on #1a1a1f cards; the single purple accent is rationed to buttons, links, toggles and one gradient-framed sync panel. Rhythm alternates alignment section by section — left-aligned hero, split claim-stack, centered bento, text/mock splits, a centered CTA — before closing on a dense five-column footer.

records.name: Obsidian Open Graph social card by obsidian.md
records.description: A 1200×630 social card built on a near-black canvas with one horizontal lockup placed left of centre: a dark rounded-square app icon holding a faceted purple gem, a large white bold wordmark, and a lavender-purple tagline beneath it. Hierarchy comes purely from scale and colour — the white display type reads first, the purple subline second, the gem icon anchors the left edge. The right third is left as empty, faintly textured darkness, so the mark stays legible even at tiny share sizes.

records.name: Oku book-tracking app landing page by oku.club
records.description: A near-monochrome landing page on warm paper white: a high-contrast serif carries every headline while a neutral sans handles body copy and UI, with solid black pill CTAs as the only strong accent. Feature sections alternate full-width light-gray panels with pairs of half-width cards, and phone/browser mockups deliberately bleed off and get clipped by the panel edges. Personality comes entirely from black-ink hand-drawn illustration — a hero reader, circular team portraits, scattered books on a curved pre-CTA divider — while the only colour on the page arrives through content imagery like book covers; rhythm winds down through a white social-proof block, a full-bleed community activity strip, definition-style Q&A rows and a curved finale.

records.name: Oku reading app social card by oku.club
records.description: A monochrome ink-on-paper social card built on an asymmetric split: a small serif lockup and a two-line serif headline (~72–80px) anchor the left half, while a grainy hand-inked illustration of a lounging reader and an open book bleeds off the right edge. Only two values are used — warm off-white paper and near-black ink — and there is no chrome, gradient or footer, so the card reads like a page from a book and stays legible at chat-preview thumbnail sizes.

records.name: Omnea — Agentic OS for Procurement landing page by omnea.co
records.description: A long editorial enterprise landing page built almost entirely in a warm off-white/beige palette with near-black serif headlines. The hero is minimal — centred type, a single dark pill CTA and a faint dot-matrix motif — followed by a quiet grey logo strip. The page alternates rhythm: dense bento feature grids with UI mockups, a full-bleed dark "agent" section that resets the eye, large stat blocks set in oversized serif numerals, editorial photography with pull-quotes, geometric line-drawn trust/compliance tiles, and finally a testimonial wall, article cards, newsletter capture and a dark closing CTA with a big footer. Small uppercase eyebrow labels with dots organise every section, giving a consistent navigational rhythm despite the varied content.

records.name: Omnea 'The Agentic OS for Procurement' social card by omnea.co
records.description: The card is a single typographic statement on a warm cream field: a two-line high-contrast serif headline set at roughly 150px dominates the 1200×630 canvas, with no logo competing for attention. Four white pill chips ('Mitigation Agent', '4th Party Agent', etc.) are scattered asymmetrically around the type — top-right, mid-left, lower-right, bottom-centre — each pairing an uppercase monospace label with a small halftone dot orb in muted red, blue or green, the only saturated colour on the card. Chips slightly overlap the headline's edges, creating a shallow depth that makes the static card feel like agents orbiting the product claim.

records.name: OpenTable homepage — restaurant reservation hub by opentable.com
records.description: A utility-first reservation homepage that leads with a pill-shaped search bar (date, time, party size, location) and a red CTA, then settles into image-led card carousels where every card repeats the same anatomy: photo, bookmark, name, star rating, cuisine/price/neighborhood meta line, social proof, and an outlined 'find next available' button. Red (#DA3743) is the only saturated colour on white until the page's chapter breaks — a soft mint-to-peach AI prompt banner mid-page and a saturated orange-red-purple gradient banner for restaurateurs near the end. Density is high in the card rows, opens up through the illustrated FAQ and three-column city-link grid, and the page closes with a dark navy five-column footer, giving the scroll a clear card-row → editorial → utility → footer rhythm.

records.name: outbid.lol — pay-to-rank product leaderboard by outbid.lol
records.description: A pay-to-rank leaderboard where the design gamifies scarcity: one hot-orange accent marks everything money-related — bid prices, active pills, the claim button — while the rest of the page stays near-monochrome. The hero compresses pitch and action into a single row (a live bid price with tiny steppers, a URL input, a category select, a claim button), then hands off to a dense 50-row feed in which the top three ranks are tinted peach, a live-activity strip interrupts after #10, and a 'TOP 20' pill divider resets the rhythm before progressively quieter mid-table rows finish in numbered pagination. Fully-rounded pill controls, tabular rank numerals, 12px meta labels and hairline dividers keep 2,870 products scannable; a compact sidebar mini-ranking and a three-card stats band close the page.

records.name: Partiful party-invite landing page by partiful.com
records.description: A consumer event-invite landing page that sells joy through motion and photography rather than feature lists. The hero sets the tone: an oversized two-line white headline over a purple-to-blue gradient, candid flash photography, and a floating RSVP card doing product-demo duty. Down the page a continuous pastel gradient canvas shifts hue every few sections while the rhythm alternates between airy centered statements and dense split feature rows; rotated UI mockups, emoji-punctuated headings, black pill CTAs, press-quote and photo-collage palate cleansers, app-store ratings, a three-card blog teaser, and a five-column footer close the loop.

records.name: Partiful party invitations OG card by partiful.com
records.description: A 1200×630 social card built around a fanned cluster of three tilted invitation cards floating over a dark aubergine gradient. Each card follows the same anatomy — big date headline at the top, a photo or motif panel in the middle, event title in large type at the bottom — while their distinct palettes (icy blue, pixel-sprinkled indigo, peach-to-pink gradient) create variety within repetition. Glossy translucent bubbles, soft bokeh circles and two magenta glow orbs add depth around the edges, keeping the dark background atmospheric without competing with the cards.

records.name: Patreon creator platform landing page by patreon.com
records.description: The page uses a cinematic, editorial landing-page structure: a full-bleed photographic hero with oversized white typography gives way to pale blue and saturated blue product-story sections. Large type, asymmetrical image collages, testimonial photography, and floating interface mockups create a changing rhythm from emotional storytelling to concrete product capabilities, while black pill buttons and a dense black footer provide consistent anchors.

records.name: Patreon OG social card by patreon.com
records.description: A 1200×630 card built around a single full-bleed photograph: a near-black floral backdrop with deep reds and mossy greens, and the subject placed on the right third gazing off-canvas left, which pulls the eye back toward the type. The headline is an oversized, light-weight grotesque set in white across two staggered lines that fill the lower half, overlapping the subject with no knockout because the photography is dark enough to hold the contrast. The only other element is a small all-caps wordmark in the bottom-left corner, so brand, message and image form exactly three layers.

records.name: Peerspace landing page by peerspace.com
records.description: Peerspace's homepage alternates hard colour blocks — black hero, deep-violet awards banner, white category section, black filmstrip and city list, cream editorial breaks — each anchored by large credited photography like 'Production — Super8 studio, Houston TX'. Scale contrast carries the hierarchy: 100px+ grotesque headlines sit against 11px uppercase micro-labels and tiny state/country captions. Interaction is photo-led throughout: a floating three-field search card rides the hero, the activity tag cloud swaps the adjacent image, the dimmed grey city list brightens on hover, and carousels use thin arrows with 01/03 counters.

records.name: Phantom — crypto wallet & trading homepage by phantom.com
records.description: Phantom's homepage pairs a soft lavender shell with a full-bleed gray hero video and then organises everything below into three labelled bento sections — Trading, Move Money, Your security — each a horizontal carousel of tall feature cards. Each card is a self-contained colour world (purple, dark, mint, blue, pink, yellow) with a short benefit headline and a rich product illustration or UI mock, so colour, not typography, carries the hierarchy. The page closes with a giant serif "Get started. Download Phantom." statement, legal small print, and a rounded footer with newsletter signup and status indicator.

records.name: Phantom social card by phantom.com
records.description: A 1200×630 social card uses a nearly full-bleed lavender-purple canvas with a single centered horizontal lockup. The white abstract mark sits to the left of a large lowercase wordmark, creating a strong focal band with generous negative space above and below; the treatment is flat, unbordered, and free of secondary copy or imagery.

records.name: Pitch presentation workspace landing page by pitch.com
records.description: A long-form marketing page that moves from a luminous, lavender AI hero into spacious white product-story sections, then increases density with metrics, a horizontal workflow showcase, testimonial cards, and a bento-like toolkit grid. Purple is the signature colour, appearing as soft gradients and UI accents on white before becoming a deep full-bleed background for solutions, templates, and FAQs; neon lime buttons and cards provide contrast, while oversized rounded product mockups and restrained black typography keep the page approachable and editorial.

records.name: Pitch purple social card by pitch.com
records.description: A 1200×630 social card uses a full-bleed violet-to-blue gradient with a subtle darker center, leaving generous negative space around a centered white wordmark. The compact brand mark sits directly left of the large rounded sans-serif name, creating one strong horizontal focal unit with no supporting copy, imagery, borders, or interface chrome.

records.name: Plaid fintech homepage by plaid.com
records.description: The page opens and closes with the same cyan-to-blue gradient atmosphere, wrapping a rhythm of light product sections and deep-navy rounded banner blocks. An engraved banknote illustration with magenta halftone overlays gives the brand a tactile signature, while pastel bento product cards, a purple serif stat grid, floating notification cards, and a dark code-editor mockup shift the tone from marketing to technical proof. A dense multi-column navy footer with generous rounding closes the page.

records.name: PlanetScale cloud database platform homepage by planetscale.com
records.description: The page reads like a printed technical spec: one monospace family carries everything from the yellow announcement bar to the footer, and hierarchy comes from bold, underlines and 1px table borders rather than size jumps or decoration. The hero is a short statement with a red accent bar, then the page spends its length on a huge bordered logo wall, a tabbed product section illustrated with an ASCII architecture diagram, and man-page-style sections (Performance, Uptime, Cost, Security, Features) separated by dotted rules and punctuated with attributed quotes. Colour is rationed — yellow promo bar, orange-red CTA and accent bar, blue/green inline links on an otherwise black-and-white page — which makes the sparse accents and the ASCII diagram feel intentional rather than plain.

records.name: PlanetScale dark social-proof OG card by planetscale.com
records.description: A 1200×630 social card built almost entirely from typographic trust signals on a near-black canvas with a faint dot-grid texture. Hierarchy is a strict three-tier centered stack: a large white wordmark with its circular mark, a widely-tracked monospace uppercase tagline in mid-gray, then a 5×4 wall of customer wordmarks set in flat muted gray. Every logo is forced into the same grayscale so the composition reads as one texture, and the bottom row is cropped by the canvas edge with reduced opacity, implying the list continues beyond the frame.

records.name: PostHog homepage — playful analytics landing page by posthog.com
records.description: The page runs on a single cream canvas with one narrow centred text column, alternating short copy blocks with right-aligned ink-drawn hedgehog illustrations so every section reads as text-plus-character. Hierarchy comes from oversized black sans headings that each carry exactly one blue keyword, yellow highlighter marks behind key phrases, and 1px-bordered white cards (logo wall, pricing table, parody shop) that spike the density against otherwise airy sections. The hero and footer bookend the page with retro-game touches — an illustrated grass-world navigation rail with chalkboard icon shortcuts, a blue-framed tabbed product demo, and a self-aware fake e-commerce card that closes the page on a joke.

records.name: PostHog social card — desktop-window composition by posthog.com
records.description: A 1200×630 social card that stages PostHog's desktop-OS landing metaphor: a full-bleed sage-green low-poly landscape with a thin browser-chrome strip and orange CTA pill, plus a floating cream window carrying the lockup, a heavy black headline with a blue selection-highlight phrase, and a nested get-started panel containing a two-tone monospace command chip. Focal order reads wordmark → headline → highlighted phrase → command chip, while small labelled shortcut icons flank the window to sustain the OS conceit. Flat shapes, large radii, a single soft shadow and roughly three colours (sage, cream, ink) keep the card legible even at thumbnail size.

records.name: Prisma homepage — TypeScript ORM, Postgres & hosting by prisma.io
records.description: A white canvas with near-black display type, black pill CTAs and soft pastel gradient washes (mint-to-pink) that frame the hero, product mockups and closing CTA, punctuated by Prisma's cyan/yellow/coral ribbon motif. The page alternates rhythm down its length: a centered hero with a console mockup, a grayscale logo band, a before/after comparison pair, three tinted step cards, alternating product rows linked by file-chip connectors, a tabbed cost-comparison card, a testimonial grid, a FAQ accordion, and a gradient CTA card before a light footer that ends in a giant cropped wordmark. Hierarchy is carried almost entirely by type scale and hairline-bordered white cards, keeping dense product information airy.

records.name: Prisma OG social card by prisma.io
records.description: A 1200×630 light social card built almost entirely from negative space: a small mark-plus-wordmark lockup sits top-left, a three-line headline in a dark warm-gray rounded geometric sans dominates the left half at roughly 96–110px, and a fan of teal, yellow and coral stripes slices diagonally through the lower-right corner, softened by a blurred warm glow. Brand colour is quarantined in the mark and the stripe motif, so the type carries the message while the single diagonal injects momentum. Hierarchy reads in one sweep — lockup, headline, accent — with the upper-right quadrant deliberately empty.

records.name: Public investing platform homepage by public.com
records.description: Public's homepage runs on a cream canvas with an oversized high-contrast serif display face against a quiet neutral sans, and it builds rhythm by alternating full-bleed light and near-black bands. The hero is restrained — two lines of left-aligned serif, three icon callouts, one black pill CTA — then a dark annotated-device media band, followed by a purely typographic product index where dot separators and tiny yield chips carry the information. Below, AI feature blocks mix centered editorial captions with dense, realistic product mockups that let green market-data accents do the colour work; a black 'active trading' band mixes a rebate table, a 3D stat cube and syntax-highlighted code; later bands handle concierge, security trust facts in a 2×3 grid, and a conversion close with device mockups, ending in a multi-column footer with a long small-print legal block.

records.name: Public investing social card by public.com
records.description: A roughly 1200×630 social card uses a clean asymmetric split: a large black editorial serif headline occupies the white left half, while a rounded black image panel anchors the right. A trading dashboard and phone are layered inside the panel with a cool blue foreground glow; the small lowercase wordmark sits at bottom left, creating a restrained fintech composition with strong focal hierarchy.

records.name: Railway cloud platform landing page by railway.com
records.description: A near-black, long-scroll landing page that pairs an editorial serif display face with monospace UI labels, set against a vaporwave illustrated hero (starry sky, gradient mountains, train). The page runs on a repeating 'chapter' skeleton — monospace eyebrow tag, serif heading, one-line support copy with a Learn more arrow, a large product screenshot, a 3-up blurb row, and an 'Alternative to' competitor icon row — so rhythm comes from repetition while section backgrounds subtly shift tint (deep green for observability, deep purple elsewhere) to mark transitions. Dense, hairline-bordered logo wall and monospace flip-counter stats provide contrast to the airy feature sections, with purple reserved almost exclusively for the primary CTA and green for status/success states.

records.name: Railway OG social card — 'Ship Without Friction' by railway.com
records.description: A 1200×630 social card on a near-black canvas with a faint dot-grid texture. The composition splits into two zones: a static type block on the left (small wordmark lockup top-left, a three-line all-caps heavy headline anchored bottom-left) and a dynamic product visual on the right two-thirds — isometric service cards (backend, frontend, redis, postgres) connected by glowing purple deployment lines that bleed off the canvas edges. It works because of that diagonal tension between quiet typography and a cropped, depth-cued product render, with colour discipline: white type, muted greys, purple glow as the only loud accent plus tiny green status checks.

records.name: Ramp landing page by ramp.com
records.description: A long, calm fintech landing page built almost entirely from a warm off-white canvas, black editorial typography and a single acid-yellow accent. Hierarchy comes from very large serif-adjacent display headlines alternating with small utility labels, and rhythm shifts from a tight hero with an inline email capture into spacious bento feature cards, a soft photographic testimonial band, then a wide testimonial grid that accelerates density before a minimal email-only CTA and an unusually detailed dark legal footer. Product UI screenshots float on the same cream background with no heavy chrome, letting real interface fragments act as the imagery.

records.name: Ramp open graph social card by ramp.com
records.description: A 1200×630 social card that works like a product collage rather than a billboard: the black wordmark anchors the empty left third, a large dark credit card with concentric-line texture forms the focal centre, and a right rail of small app UI vignettes (transaction row, stacked-area chart, reimbursement pill, spending progress) plus a currency-conversion chip fill the frame with believable product evidence. Hierarchy is built by scale contrast — one hero object, then small tiles at decreasing importance — while a warm light-grey canvas, white tiles and sparse yellow/green accents keep the busy composition calm. Type is a single grotesque sans used at drastically different sizes, from display wordmark down to 11px UI labels.

records.name: Ravio compensation benchmarking landing page by Ravio
records.description: An editorial landing page on a warm cream canvas where a high-contrast serif carries the hero, section headings and oversized stat numerals, while a quiet sans handles nav, body and UI labels. Rhythm alternates between airy centred-text sections and dense data moments — a tabbed product screenshot on tinted panels, a hairline-divided stats band, a testimonial triptych with portrait photography, and a two-card bento explainer — before a near-black footer flips the palette. Colour stays disciplined (cream, ink black, one blue accent plus pink/yellow chart tints), and faint spreadsheet-style hairlines serve as both background texture and section dividers.

records.name: Raycast 2.0 launch page by Raycast 2.0
records.description: The page runs on a near-black canvas where white display type and pill-shaped CTA buttons are the only high-contrast elements; all product UI is shown as tilted 3D renders that dissolve into the background via gradient masks. Rhythm alternates between oversized centered statements, a quiet numbered 01–03 row that sets upgrade expectations, and a mid-page bento grid of dark UI cards with captions pinned bottom-left. It closes by mirroring the hero ('The launcher, relaunched.') and then opens into a six-column footer on a slightly lighter surface with a newsletter bar.

records.name: Raycast 2.0 launch social card by Raycast 2.0
records.description: A 1200×630 launch card on a near-black stage. A small monochrome glyph sits top-centre, the two-line white headline dominates the middle with heavy sans type, and a 3D perspective render of the command bar rises from the bottom edge, dimmed into the background so only the nearest rows (icons, command labels, an 'Open Application' action chip) read clearly. Depth is achieved by fading the UI mockup into black rather than by decoration, with one warm red/orange glow on the left of the mockup as the only accent.

records.name: Raycast landing page by raycast.com
records.description: A near-black single-column page that opens with a huge centred hero, then alternates short manifesto statements with oversized product screenshots floating on red-orange radial glows. Mid-page the rhythm shifts to dense, colour-coded content: app-branded extension cards (indigo, blue, green), an AI window with chat suggestion chips, avatar-driven testimonials, and a developer bento grid filled with wireframe-blue isometric illustrations, closing on a giant 3D keyboard render and a six-column mega footer. Everything is disciplined single-sans typography on #0b0b0d, with the red gradient reserved for glows, eyebrows and emphasis, so colour is earned, not sprayed.

records.name: Raycast social card — dark command palette OG image by raycast.com
records.description: A 1200×630 social card that reads as one vertical stack on a near-black stage: centered wordmark, a single oversized gradient headline, and a command-palette app window that bleeds off the bottom edge. All colour is environmental — diagonal red light streaks rake across the backdrop and rim-light the window's border, so the UI itself stays monochrome glass. Focal hierarchy is achieved purely through scale and position: type at the top does the talking, the product shot below proves it.

records.name: Relic clipboard vault landing page by Relic
records.description: A warm, paper-toned long-scroll landing page for a clipboard manager, built on cream/beige backgrounds with a signature mustard-yellow accent. Hierarchy comes from pairing a clean grotesque with italic serif accent words ("no place", "Summon it anywhere.") that carry the brand voice through every section heading. Rhythm alternates between full-bleed product screenshots (dark app UI on a yellow gradient card), three-up feature cards, a five-column platform grid, a story timeline, a compact bento of "small things", a dark inverted privacy section, a four-tier pricing row, and an accordion FAQ — so density and background shift every couple of viewports to keep the long scroll fresh. Small mono uppercase section labels (01 CAPTURE, 06 · END-TO-END ENCRYPTED) add editorial structure throughout.

records.name: Relic Open Graph social card by Relic
records.description: A 1200×630 social card split into a quiet typographic left column and a tactile paper collage on the right. The top-left locks up an amber rounded-triangle mark with the wordmark and a black OPEN SOURCE pill; the headline sets two lines in a heavy geometric sans before pivoting to a high-contrast italic serif for the final phrase in amber — the card's strongest colour moment. The right half layers stationery ephemera (handwritten list, napkin, receipt, business card, polaroid) with soft directional shadows, topped by a translucent amber version of the logo object acting as the brand anchor, while a small letterspaced amber domain line closes the bottom-left.

records.name: Render cloud platform homepage by render.com
records.description: A light, grid-disciplined cloud-infrastructure landing page that persuades with real product UI rather than decoration. The hero pairs an oversized grotesque headline with a mock deployment panel (service cards, sparklines, a '$ git push' mono chip) over faint grid lines. Below the hero the rhythm alternates between airy white sections and tinted full-bleed bands: a quiet monochrome logo wall, a numbered three-step flow illustrated with UI fragments, a saturated purple stack band, then a lavender bento grid where cards alternate text-plus-mockup layouts and switch chart colour from violet to green. It closes with sparse icon-led capability and security grids, a playful floating-tile CTA, and a dense black footer with a pixel motif. One violet accent, black rectangular CTAs, hairline borders, and mono type for terminal labels hold the whole page together.

records.name: Render 'Your fastest path to production' OG card by render.com
records.description: A dark share card that splits the canvas into a quiet typographic left half and a decorative data-mosaic right half. A small wordmark anchors the top-left corner while a three-line white headline in a light geometric sans carries all the focal weight. The right side is a bleeding grid of hairline-outlined dark tiles, a few filled with purple-to-mint gradients striped with horizontal bars that read as abstracted terminal output.

records.name: Replicate AI infrastructure landing page by replicate.com
records.description: A long-form AI developer landing page moves from a vivid pink-purple-yellow gradient hero into practical product proof: a live code-and-output demo, pill filters, horizontal model cards, contributor avatars, and a centered community statement. The middle shifts to a bordered white technical explainer with stacked run, fine-tuning, and deployment modules, then to a dark enterprise section with orange chart treatments and dense two-column capability cards; it finishes with an oversized editorial “Imagine what you can build” collage, gradient divider lines, and a restrained multi-column footer.

records.name: Resend developer email platform landing page by resend.com
records.description: A near-black developer landing page built on a repeating chapter rhythm: each product claim is introduced by a glossy 3D icon and a centred serif heading with an italic orange accent phrase, then immediately proven with a real artifact — a tabbed code window, a code/live-preview split, or an actual product screenshot. Hierarchy comes from a high-contrast serif display face (roman and italic mixed at ~90px) over a small muted grotesque body, with density swinging between airy section intros and dense utilitarian blocks: a 13-icon SDK row, a 3×3 deliverability grid, and bordered cards containing mock-UI states. Colour discipline holds the page together — #0a0a0a canvas, white headlines, #a1a1aa body, orange #ff5a1f reserved for accent italics, green and red confined to semantic statuses — flowing through a monochrome logo wall, a single anchor testimonial, a three-card quote grid, and a five-column footer.

records.name: Resend "Email for Developers" OG social card by resend.com
records.description: A 1200×630 social card on a near-black canvas with faint diagonal light streaks rising from the lower corners. The composition is one centered column: a rounded app-icon tile, an oversized high-contrast serif headline with a subtle silver-to-white fade, and a dark code-editor mockup that bleeds off the bottom edge to imply more content below. It stays strictly monochrome — white keywords and muted gray syntax on charcoal panels with hairline borders — so the serif headline carries all the visual weight.

records.name: Resurf landing page — personal context library for Mac by Resurf
records.description: An editorial-minimal landing page where hierarchy comes almost entirely from type: oversized serif display headlines sit above tiny gray sans-serif body copy on a warm off-white canvas, while all UI chrome (nav, buttons, cards, footer) stays monochrome so the only colour arrives inside the product screenshots. The page builds rhythm by alternating centred headline blocks with large framed visuals: hero → full-width Mac window screenshot → a 3×4 bento of feature tiles, each with a miniature white UI mockup and a one-line description → a tabbed product tour with a segmented control → an icon grid of supported formats → an overlapping desktop/phone/tablet collage → a centred CTA and a whisper-quiet footer. Pill buttons, 16px tile radii, flat tonal fills instead of borders, and small 'Opt-in' meta badges keep everything calm and native-Mac feeling.

records.name: Rocket Money fintech landing page by rocketmoney.com
records.description: A consumer fintech landing page built on a white canvas with large light-gray rounded panels that break the rhythm into distinct acts: hero, social proof, three alternating feature stories, a free-vs-premium comparison, a 2×2 feature grid, and a masonry review wall. Hierarchy is carried by a single rounded geometric sans scaled dramatically down the page (hero ≈64px → section heads ≈40px → 16px body), while CTA weight steps down from a black pill in the hero to outlined pills beside each feature to plain underlined links in the grid. Warm lifestyle photography with floating white UI cards (subscriptions, alerts, savings goals) sits against the flat panels, and a single crimson red is rationed for icons, stars, progress bars and the app header, keeping the page feeling calm, editorial and trustworthy despite its density.

records.name: Rocket Money OG social card by rocketmoney.com
records.description: A 1200×630 share card built on a quiet warm-gray canvas with a hard left/right split: a text lockup on the left, a cropped device hero on the right. Hierarchy is pure scale — red wordmark, then a two-line near-black display headline, then three gray bullets — while all the colour energy (crimson gradient header, purple chart, green checkmarks) is pushed into the phone screen. The ~30° rotated phone bleeding off the top and bottom edges gives the card depth and motion without any background decoration.

records.name: Runway landing page by runwayml.com
records.description: A cinematic, monochrome landing page where full-bleed imagery does the persuading and a neutral grotesque with tight tracking carries the copy. The page alternates between airy white sections (partner strip, three-column platform grid, tabbed showcase, 2×2 news grid) and two immersive bands — a misty forest hero with left-aligned white type and a blurred olive-green research band with hairline-divided link lists. Everything is flat and shadow-free: hierarchy comes from a strong scale jump (56px display → 14px body), bold-vs-regular weight, and gray secondary text, while buttons stay in three quiet tiers (black filled, light-gray filled, white/outline on imagery) and a dense black link-column footer closes the page.

records.name: Runway OG social card by runwayml.com
records.description: A 1200×630 social card built almost entirely from atmosphere: a soft, defocused gradient field reads like a blurred film still, sweeping from pale warm mist at the lower left into deep teal and near-black corners at the top and right. Hierarchy is carried by exactly two text elements — a single line of light-weight white grotesque headline set across the optical middle, and a small lowercase wordmark near the bottom center — with the darkened upper edge doing the legibility work so no boxes or overlays are needed. The enormous negative space and the absence of any UI, buttons or product imagery give it a cinematic, editorial restraint that suits a generative-video brand.

records.name: Sentry developer monitoring landing page by sentry.io
records.description: A deep purple-black starfield sets a space theme that carries through cartoon mascots and retro illustration, while a repeating two-tone headline pattern (white first line, hot-pink second line) gives every section the same signature. Proof is handled through bordered dark cards embedding miniature UI mockups and split sections that pair pink-ruled step lists with product screenshots ringed in pink, so dense feature content stays legible. Rhythm shifts down the page: dense feature grids give way to an airy testimonial trio, then a hands-on terminal install block, trust badges, a newsletter card, an oversized closing CTA, and a dense four-column footer.

records.name: Sentry OG social card — mascot debugging vignette by sentry.io
records.description: A 1200×630 social card built as a triptych: skeleton product vignettes (Replays and Traces timelines) bleed off the left edge, an oversized flat-vector robot fills the centre, and an AI-diagnosis card bleeds off the right. Two light beams — hot magenta from the character's ray gun toward the left panels, neon lime from its handheld scanner toward the right panel — act as focal connectors, so the mascot literally illuminates the product UI it is debugging. The deep purple-black canvas carries saturated magenta/purple character art and reserves a single lime accent for headings and key UI spans, with white bold sans headings and small icon-chipped event lines adding technical texture.

records.name: SHIUI Hinomaru Ink UI kit catalogue by SHIUI
records.description: A long-form component catalogue uses an off-white paper ground, hairline gray rules, condensed uppercase metadata, and a restrained vermilion accent to evoke a printed Japanese editorial system. The page moves from a framed hero and token swatches into increasingly dense two-column specimen grids: buttons and tags, forms, navigation, feedback, data, overlays, cards, marks, and charts, with each specimen boxed, labeled, and annotated for reuse.

records.name: Speechmark — private on-device meeting notes landing page by Speechmark
records.description: A privacy-first Mac app landing page built almost entirely on typographic craft rather than illustration. A serif headline system (large roman + italic blue emphasis lines) pairs with small tracked sans eyebrows ('— HOW IT WORKS') to label each band, while the page alternates white and pale blue-grey sections with two deliberate colour breaks: a saturated blue full-bleed testimonial and a dark navy closing CTA and footer. Content devices stay restrained and consistent — numbered 01–03 columns with hairline dividers, a minimal comparison table whose Speechmark column is highlighted with blue pill checks, a Mac-vs-cloud privacy diagram using a filled card against a dashed one, and a single-open FAQ accordion. A faint audio waveform strip anchors the hero, the only decorative motif, echoed later as small waveform graphics inside the privacy diagram.

records.name: Speechmark Open Graph social card by Speechmark
records.description: The card is essentially the app icon enlarged: a warm off-white macOS-style squircle floats on a full-bleed near-black field, carrying a single oversized opening-quote glyph optically centred slightly above the tile's middle. There is no headline, wordmark or URL — focal hierarchy comes entirely from the scale jump between one glyph and the surrounding negative space, plus the cream-on-black luminance contrast. A faint top-to-bottom sheen on the tile makes it read as a physical icon, and the strict two-value palette keeps it legible even at thumbnail size.

records.name: Stowdrop landing page by stowdrop.app
records.description: A long dark landing page for a Mac clipboard/snippet app built almost entirely on near-black surfaces with a single orange accent used for eyebrows, key words and CTA buttons. The page opens with a centered hero over a subtle radial glow and an app-window screenshot of the actual library UI, then alternates between full-width feature statements and bento-style cards showing UI panels, tiles and real product photography. Typography is large sans headings with tight leading and per-line alternating emphasis (one word picked out in orange), while body copy stays small and muted gray. Sections step down in rhythm from hero to feature bento rows, a stats band, a keyboard-shortcut table, an FAQ accordion, and a final CTA card, all separated by hairline borders and generous dark spacing.

records.name: Strawberry AI browser landing page by strawberrybrowser.com
records.description: A long, softly cream-toned landing page that pairs Apple-style product marketing (huge centred hero headline, large product screenshot, logo strip) with playful pastel mascot characters that recur throughout as a visual thread. Below the hero the rhythm alternates: full-width centred statements, a two-column bento grid of feature cards with embedded UI mockups, a use-case carousel of mini browser windows, a three-column onboarding strip, a large composited screenshot section, a 3x2 testimonial grid, a security section, a chat-bubble FAQ (the answer styled as a dark chat message), and a final CTA with repeated logo marquee and multi-column footer. Typography is a big grotesque scale — very large display headings against small, generous grey body copy — and the warm off-white background with hairline card borders keeps everything feeling light and friendly despite the density.

records.name: Stripe homepage — financial infrastructure landing page by stripe.com
records.description: The page runs a strict two-colour system — white canvas with navy #0A2540 text and blurple #635BFF accents — and lets huge 3D gradient artwork (orange→pink→purple) do the expressive work in the hero, then resets to restraint below. Rhythm alternates down the page: a bento grid of product cards each embedding a real UI screenshot, a full-bleed dark event banner, an airy stat band with a radial particle graphic, photographic case studies, and finally a long navy developer section with node diagrams, animated wave gradients and a code snippet. Hierarchy is carried almost entirely by type scale (60px+ display, 24px section intros, 14px gray captions) and by weight rather than ornament, with pills, 1px borders and gradient washes instead of shadows.

records.name: Stripe gradient wordmark social card by stripe.com
records.description: A 1200×630 brand card built almost entirely from one gesture: a diagonal silk-like gradient sweep running from a cool lavender/periwinkle anchor in the lower-left through hot pink at mid-left into a saturated orange mass filling the upper right, with streaked anisotropic bands rather than a smooth CSS-style blend. The white extra-bold lowercase wordmark is the sole element, centered a touch above the vertical midpoint at roughly a third of the canvas width, so the entire focal hierarchy rests on colour field versus type contrast. There is no headline, tagline or framing device — the negative space and the diagonal motion do the communicating, which keeps the card legible at feed-thumbnail size.

records.name: Supabase product platform landing page by supabase.com
